A1C09E52FCF94DABA04E9EA21FE588D5.description: Distinguish among fact, opinion, and reasoned judgment in a text.

5D0543C7477D45E9B6CA02AD7CD68717.description: Integrate visual information (e.g., in charts, graphs, photographs, videos, or maps) with other information in print and digital texts.

86D3ABC924534DE781217A0A3AC54912.description: Identify aspects of a text that reveal an author's point of view or purpose (e.g., loaded language, inclusion or avoidance of particular facts).

9932911195F04555A273BBABD139688F.description: Describe how a text presents information (e.g., sequentially, comparatively, causally).

5F0A9496F35143DBB7BF00C30C1312BE.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including vocabulary specific to domains related to history/social studies.

AD67981A31C64C07A11923CADE763EA2.description: Identify key steps in a text's description of a process related to history/social studies (e.g., how a bill becomes law, how interest rates are raised or lowered).

51BAFA92F0574D17811A3F3CE0B55F50.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of the source distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

62D37A88D02340738F3EEDDD4A2C254C.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources.

6B8F8E1918FF454786E7B20F08BEF09A.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

9D654D5174BA4853852010F6EC1A8D7C.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6—8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

E186B9556D5645C99A1FA13320172518.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

349B6B1CBDF74074BAADE8E5E12CC80C.description: Compare and contrast one author's presentation of events with that of another (e.g., a memoir written by and a biography on the same person).

C3552C0F9B3342BCADCF2ECFC5F85B4A.description: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

DDBA58D0E58140B5B2040BC6575FE64D.description: Integrate information presented in different media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively) as well as in words to develop a coherent understanding of a topic or issue.

E2DD510B42E041D2AE40CB47FD1A6E07.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and explain how it is conveyed in the text.

7BBB2AF6DE2A4FDBA6E64A2B93B00BBD.description: Analyze how a particular sentence, paragraph, chapter, or section fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the ideas.

70DDF1111C634632AD4CD36C8991BD90.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings.

0625CBAF020045E187D6DB0F68BA317F.description: Analyze in detail how a key individual, event, or idea is introduced, illustrated, and elaborated in a text (e.g., through examples or anecdotes).

AE595EEABB064FBDB409E034547B28DD.description: Determine a central idea of a text and how it is conveyed through particular details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.

5A28F9343C194461BEAC04CD75A6EB80.description: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

4B66571406A246D895B8CA832714A64A.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 6—8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

A3DB53A2248B4C59A1ABBD28C4C29A2C.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

FAB39187BDD046D1A2B163D1EF7B757A.description: Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres (e.g., stories and poems; historical novels and fantasy stories) in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics.

0CE1D97E7F004273930BEF3A1EF0A627.description: Compare and contrast the experience of reading a story, drama, or poem to listening to or viewing an audio, video, or live version of the text, including contrasting what they "see" and "hear" when reading the text to what they perceive when they listen or watch.

DA71A88A86D6486A891BC35522877F86.description: Explain how an author develops the point of view of the narrator or speaker in a text.

CB2E0DD2534A46A9A9F3481869D5F95A.description: Analyze how a particular sentence, chapter, scene, or stanza fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the theme, setting, or plot.

DE9036279CF74EA1A8E033C3C4ADBDCB.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.

FA458A2463494D4DAADD9E5328514550.description: Describe how a particular story's or drama's plot unfolds in a series of episodes as well as how the characters respond or change as the plot moves toward a resolution.

D02269F637CC4EE6B894B644C41164C0.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and how it is conveyed through particular details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.

E81E1E22387A4D76BF08D5EF48521DA4.description: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

1B82F2309132483593E120044C09E1FE.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

82C3CE3E6E29430F823405569D6A0A00.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

CB348BDC11124EE398DFCFA1692C73F7.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

67E0718140F842609C1EFA249DDC5F0E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

051F354E08654F0089EFEB6DB4489615.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

700303AE063C413AB26201C3ADA4472B.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

75F29BCEBE4243498BF79AB50337D83B.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

3EB560388DF54CD584A53DAD5DC1F4A2.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

4FB5E4C17D5544A9BC16CB1BEAE6B8F0.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

339ED806CD29487F8766C074EBAB41C7.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

3A396D76B93A4A5B9E4CD47CED153721.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

0CDC5A7BEFD94B6B8556877D28C0FA7E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

CEFE2C40DFE7013130C768A86D17958E.description: Summarize personal preferences in music selections according to their excellence of performance, meaning/purpose, and use of music elements.

CEFDE450DFE7013130C668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate familiarity with suggested listening selections.

CEFDA410DFE7013130C568A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the differences between a band and an orchestra, the vocal timbres of soprano, alto, tenor, bass, quartet, and the instrumental timbres of the English horn, bass clarinet, saxophones, sousaphone, harp, piccolo, and categorize in timbral families.

CEFD6400DFE7013130C468A86D17958E.description: Identify by sight and sound and categorize into instrument families the English horn, bass clarinet, saxophone, sousaphone, harp, and piccolo.

CEFD2200DFE7013130C368A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the textures used in familiar songs and listening selections.

CEFCDCE0DFE7013130C268A86D17958E.description: Explain how the music can communicate a certain meaning or serve a specific purpose.

CEFC9090DFE7013130C168A86D17958E.description: Explain, demonstrate, and judge own ability to exhibit appropriate audience etiquette according to type of musical performance.

CEF40D40DFE7013130C068A86D17958E.description: Perceive and respond to the messages in music and the use of music elements.

CEF33960DFE7013130BD68A86D17958E.description: Examine personal success and the achievement of others in the following: stage presence; watching the conductor; keeping a steady beat; singing in a voice free from strain; using proper playing and handling techniques of instruments; performing correct volume, pitch, and rhythm; starting and stopping together.

CEF3C850DFE7013130BF68A86D17958E.description: Plan, practice, self-assess, refine, present, and reflect on a simple performance that demonstrates all of the skills learned in each of the standards.

CEF37B80DFE7013130BE68A86D17958E.description: Formulate suggestions for improvement in music performances referring to the skills listed above.

CEF2F890DFE7013130BC68A86D17958E.description: Recognize quality while creating a music performance.

CEF2B780DFE7013130BB68A86D17958E.description: Listening: The student will listen to, analyze, and describe music.

CEF27370DFE7013130BA68A86D17958E.description: Explain the use of key signatures or how to locate do on the staff.

CEF223E0DFE7013130B968A86D17958E.description: Identify and explain unison, half steps, whole steps, and sharps/flats in melodies and pitch patterns notated on staff.

CEF1DB20DFE7013130B868A86D17958E.description: Explain sixteenths, half notes, dotted half notes; 2/4, 3/4, and 4/4 meter and the subsequent bar lines and measures in rhythm patterns.

CEF182B0DFE7013130B768A86D17958E.description: Notate as a class shorty rhythm and pitch patterns created by the teacher, individuals, and the class.

CEF14420DFE7013130B668A86D17958E.description: Use the staff system to document arrangements and compositions limited rhythmically to beamed sets of 4 sixteenth notes, whole note/rest, half note/rest, dotted half note, quarter note/rest, and eighth note pairs; and limited melodically to ti, fa, do, re, mi, so, la.

CEF04160DFE7013130B268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast creating texture in music with creating texture in other things; e.g., visual arts, dance, drama, literature.

CEEFFAF0DFE7013130B168A86D17958E.description: Build and demonstrate a simple folk instrument to provide sound effects for any of the above projects.

CEEFADE0DFE7013130B068A86D17958E.description: Create together a new song and/or a new chant ("rap").

CEEF6E30DFE7013130AF68A86D17958E.description: Create variations in the texture of a song.

CEEF2A90DFE7013130AE68A86D17958E.description: Improvise a soundtrack for a story and/or a poem.

CEEEE220DFE7013130AD68A86D17958E.description: Improvise simple rhythm and/or melody patterns to echo back and forth, and manipulate in a variety of ways to effect different textures, first with the voice and then with found sounds or instruments.

CEEEA180DFE7013130AC68A86D17958E.description: Create original music and add expression and texture to existing music.

CEF10670DFE7013130B568A86D17958E.description: Balance reason and emotion in creating, practicing, and performing.

CEF0C660DFE7013130B468A86D17958E.description: Exhibit through music an appreciation for the subtle beauties inherent in everyday life.

CEF08380DFE7013130B368A86D17958E.description: Express ideas, thoughts, and emotions aesthetically through singing, playing, and/or creating.

CEEE5E60DFE7013130AB68A86D17958E.description: Creating: The student will create music through improvising, arranging, and composing.

CEEE1580DFE7013130AA68A86D17958E.description: Determine success in playing with a sense of the texture.

CEEDB090DFE7013130A968A86D17958E.description: Rate success in playing even, dotted, and syncopated rhythm/melody patterns in echo to the teacher.

CEED5860DFE7013130A868A86D17958E.description: Judge success in playing simple melodies on the recorder or keyboard by rote and/or note reading.

CEED02A0DFE7013130A768A86D17958E.description: Evaluate success in playing with a beautiful tone, starting and stopping together, keeping a steady beat, and at indicated volume and tempo on a variety of classroom instruments.

CEECBAC0DFE7013130A668A86D17958E.description: Perform independently or with others simple melodies and accompaniments on classroom instruments.

CEEC6450DFE7013130A568A86D17958E.description: Add instrumental sounds to known songs of various cultures.

CEEBFBD0DFE7013130A468A86D17958E.description: Judge success in using proper playing and handling techniques on a variety of classroom instruments.

CEEBAEF0DFE7013130A368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate various timbres and effects of simple instruments.

CEEB7140DFE7013130A268A86D17958E.description: Discover and demonstrate sounds on simple instruments of the classroom and various cultures.

CEEB33D0DFE7013130A168A86D17958E.description: Playing: The student will play instruments as a means of musical expression.

CEEAF430DFE7013130A068A86D17958E.description: Play singing games, enjoy traditional folk dances, and patriotic songs that have originated in the cultures of the United States. Explain what they mean personally.

CEEAB090DFE70131309F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how music is used by cultures in U.S. history.

CEEA63C0DFE70131309E68A86D17958E.description: Share songs, instruments, and music enjoyed by various cultures in the history of the United States.

CEEA1F90DFE70131309D68A86D17958E.description: Discover how songs, singing games, and dances relate to various cultures in the history of the United States.

CEE925A0DFE70131309968A86D17958E.description: Rate success in reading simple pitch patterns.

CEE8E260DFE70131309868A86D17958E.description: Determine success in reading simple rhythm patterns.

CEE89990DFE70131309768A86D17958E.description: Rate success in singing an assigned part.

CEE858D0DFE70131309668A86D17958E.description: Evaluate group success in staying together, using clear enunciation, and singing in tune, expressively and in a natural voice free from strain.

CEE80E00DFE70131309568A86D17958E.description: Use the speaking and singing voice in a creative way to characterize a chosen text; e.g., manipulate pitch, volume, tempo, timbre.

CEE7C360DFE70131309468A86D17958E.description: Sing a variety of many simple songs in tune, in a natural voice, free from strain. Include descants, counter melodies, rounds, call and response, and spoken/sung accompanying chants.

CEE77790DFE70131309368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ability to sing in tune on an assigned part, with expression, accuracy, and free from strain.

CEE9E210DFE70131309C68A86D17958E.description: Show changes in meter, melodic direction, dynamics (volume), timbre, tempo, rhythm, form, mood, and texture through body movement.

CEE9A400DFE70131309B68A86D17958E.description: Explain and demonstrate the difference between beat and rhythm with body movements and rhythm games.

CEE96580DFE70131309A68A86D17958E.description: Use body movement to internalize sounds.

CEE72050DFE70131309268A86D17958E.description: Singing: The student will develop the voice and body as instruments of musical expression.

document.title: Utah Core Standards for English Language Arts

F2A2FEEAB2974688B9C4E8865C53AA2B.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

1A4394AC2C584911BFF6301B899C5948.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

99AEA241369746739F3EEB1F38584E7A.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

7AD79985250E41928F211028B00A42A2.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

B0EEE61AFD02444788AD6408BF2297AB.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

CDAC200EFEC54B8DA13B62E475DB30B7.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

54F46233A4BE44A98FE306171C843C44.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).

36E53CB6085040FAA01AC4AF6B664F4F.description: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

AB2CA02F2B5A4E5DB5D905E71F79CA95.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

5B6B033C6EE442B3A6BEA4FCE0B10133.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).

C2CEDF902C9D41F58A8AD9C395232677.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

04E9DF0AC27345F9889BFE98DD9D2748.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

BEF950A8555D46158B9577537493CF79.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

05D80430CB3A489C97524963FB470E3B.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

CE06688BDAC543079DB4707815534387.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

414BF35F3E704C4C8FE405EE22F809CD.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

E40EF3C5BCE944E7BB2DA0A0B0346414.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., to, too, two; there, their).

201622079C534BA4B29537CB5B2C5C33.description: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

700C9FDDB2FB46A6A69605C138C1E193.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (e.g., a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

8FEACBD58E6D4F8F8D102096353B01CA.description: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

5FD6325C5B7E46A9B52B32DBE59C15A2.description: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

64D33ECE6BC64F639BBC6C432B931144.description: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).

772866A783914ED9BC3F4EFD9D168613.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

00C9AB5BF0DC4827B703EB755F756B0A.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

E3D6B6A8FBB347A889598FF1EEF3AF0E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

31BA55C15FC041AAACCC29BABB989DC4.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

1AE578F1715045A2A5C5C2575A2E10E8.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

1BD98D3A14B64A2AB56AB0D16761ABCC.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

6FE470AB6A504E6690B5E26EC0BC12E0.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

EA14C502B8C543C0916CDE8846D23BD6.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

306579ACDF5B40BD94183ABDE96F8996.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

7486BD4309BD40BFAA01F3AF1CBBD530.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

E76A3CEFC9D8428ABA60A94F4B470B54.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

2F1E01FEFEDA44689D6DDD5B2EECBA37.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.

74E4E60473334FAA80178E44E0ED9D03.description: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

F02F223F74064D5CA0EDD8E54DF33DCB.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

099DA034C7644EE385455D7AB5CE4D81.description: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

8D40A18E79F74C208EB5EED1B8463EDB.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

4F28E4C1F366459C9567EDF7F038C326.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

662AECC9ACEF4C18892C0529C2AF90A8.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

1C9C2567C07741D1AF8B58E515231E13.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

E71047DDE6554933A91A5CD7FA44254C.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

15E225E1BAB447F0BBE049BC5098A353.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

2379E7DF190F487BB0D57A51A3D27D91.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

6EA5FFC4E91F4318A5592F3E973C0797.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

1B123F56A7E846EEA0D92A8D879EADD8.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

22C1F183EF23453FB4615BBCCE5ADEED.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

1FFFD111D8EA456B983E51B62E1C8428.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

697F975DB1854C51B65C20DAD6ABD1EF.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., "Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text").

B83C59590A584DBFB6C714004B2E34D6.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions].").

13FE0D0391A449EAA8965E42ACCA5C81.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

2CEDA6B59D574695BA9A6C762F87C8A3.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.

B0B9FEB24F9049F9A2CF456A14BA060A.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

158950C1A9F048CABBF8E00A318BBEC8.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

354A5DF91BE14EB7BCD4D36B41546F09.description: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.

BE5F220CE0AA4081A977A772F58A06E1.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

96227163ED6246C3B3F25D3B5A2BCF5D.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
comments: (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1—3 above.)

342698EF33AC41128811A4CE6B74C125.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

BB18C68DDA7C4A1EB167D9D0A1F1371D.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

B4BD3C3CCF9D42C68682731B1C4B6C15.description: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.

0BAE1815C40344C38EB834C00E60C252.description: Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

169F93D3DFFF495CA3FBDAA9668DBB15.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situationand introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

7FEFDE309BA540888B65143BC4652C87.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

75ED1090351C48AC9406EE106D0803B8.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented

B8B4A3C5188248108EE72C1995CB6844.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

DFC5431A21244C5380CAF5696F2CBAE9.description: Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (e.g., another, for example, also, because).

B6C2DB2B2E6C419190CB3CD2D31E36ED.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

DBB12B7D5C6044E5ABB82CA248BC9E26.description: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

05F12F86B5BF45E0B9D3817CA43FC740.description: Describe how a particular physical attribute may provide an advantage for survival in one environment but not in another (e.g., heavy fur in arctic climates keep animals warm whereas in hot desert climates it would cause overheating; flippers on such animals as sea lions and seals provide excellent swimming structures in the water but become clumsy and awkward on land; cacti retain the right amount of water in arid regions but would develop root rot in a more temperate region; fish gills have the ability to absorb oxygen in water but not on land).

90E00650756C4E1082D71D82325FEE91.description: Identify that some environments give one species a survival advantage over another (e.g., warm water favors fish such as carp, cold water favors fish such as trout, environments that burn regularly favor grasses, environments that do not often burn favor trees).

94DB22D8B26C4C83B7C25969CDF7427A.description: Compare the traits of similar species for physical abilities, instinctual behaviors, and specialized body structures that increase the survival of one species in a specific environment over another species (e.g., difference between the feet of snowshoe hare and cottontail rabbit, differences in leaves of plants growing at different altitudes, differences between the feathers of an owl and a hummingbird, differences in parental behavior among various fish).

61D5DD89FC7E42ADA7F4FE2E332094EC.description: Describe how some characteristics could give a species a survival advantage in a particular environment.

1063E91E439B474BA78035938433CC05.description: Investigate variations and similarities in plants grown from seeds of a parent plant (e.g., how seeds from the same plant species can produce different colored flowers or identical flowers).

637E0E259C824EBEA313F9A6BC4AC791.description: Contrast inherited traits with traits and behaviors that are not inherited but may be learned or induced by environmental factors (e.g., cat purring to cat meowing to be let out of the house; the round shape of a willow is inherited, while leaning away from the prevailing wind is induced).

2AEBFB0B160F46F686C87FDC0079F46B.description: Compare various examples of offspring that do not initially resemble the parent organism but mature to become similar to the parent organism (e.g., mealworms and darkling beetles, tadpoles and frogs, seedlings and vegetables, caterpillars and butterflies).

E7F0661E136E4B27881E45C936D20FA3.description: Identify similar physical traits of a parent organism and its offspring (e.g., trees and saplings, leopards and cubs, chickens and chicks).

08A9D94C00E2433B85E930BA8B200C5E.description: Make a chart and collect data identifying various traits among a given population (e.g., the hand span of students in the classroom, the color and texture of different apples, the number of petals of a given flower).

CDD7AD543E1647A0A4A94829AB34A5DC.description: Using supporting evidence, show that traits are transferred from a parent organism to its offspring.

D5364F7B5AEE4A8199E729E9C13E7ED1.description: Students will understand that traits are passed from the parent organisms to their offspring, and that sometimes the offspring may possess variations of these traits that may help or hinder survival in a given environment.

18A2919B81794386AC928C83814172FB.description: Make a working model of a complete circuit using a power source, switch, bell or light, and a conductor for a pathway.

25DB48C6C7E147FCA763EF906F4485B2.description: Investigate materials that prevent the flow of electricity.

7AC6D2324D55463D830FF68624F4131E.description: Generalize the properties of materials that carry the flow of electricity using data by testing different materials.

0900529571594C5989DF2FF39D16D0C3.description: Predict the effect of changing one or more of the components (e.g., battery, load, wires) in an electric circuit.

763DE86C0976491BAC3CB624FA22D9B2.description: Draw and label the components of a complete electrical circuit that includes switches and loads (e.g., light bulb, bell, speaker, motor).

7815F5C7E4A941B59D6465C046F7CCFF.description: Analyze the behavior of current electricity.

3F2D7F7EEDF14BD888959C2FFD72C69B.description: Investigate how various materials react differently to statically charged objects.

9BCF7A563B7542C196D176152BEECA6B.description: Compare the amount of static charge produced by rubbing various materials together (e.g., rubbing fur on a glass rod produces a greater charge then rubbing the fur with a metal rod, the static charge produced when a balloon is rubbed on hair is greater than when a plastic bag is rubbed on hair).

3BE5A0DD29AA451FA4B27540A64CC9D0.description: Describe the behavior of objects charged with static electricity in attracting or repelling without touching.

FB951B776DCC4469B7252B30EA171852.description: Describe the relationship between static electricity and lightning.

DB98B838C6AF44D9A6D416F7BF60AC66.description: List several occurrences of static electricity that happen in everyday life.

E93700E763D744CCA12916E859081DAE.description: Describe the behavior of static electricity as observed in nature and everyday occurrences.

834E99C759E04A50BE26FFF2C71CA891.description: Students will understand features of static and current electricity.

AF40E992616E46789AFF342984D6457B.description: Investigate the effects of magnets on the needle of a compass and compare this to the effects of Earth's magnetic field on the needle of a compass (e.g., magnets effect the needle only at close distances, Earth's magnetic field affects the needle at great distances, magnets close to a compass overrides the Earth's effect on the needle).

5C71EBAE70014466A536BC658629BB32.description: Construct a compass and explain how it works.

C6F3FACAAABA4533BE3A00DD35112806.description: Compare Earth's magnetic field to the magnetic field of a magnet.

0832DE66F8CB4644BB66C1088623AA6E.description: Compare the magnetic fields of various types of magnets (e.g., bar magnet, disk magnet, horseshoe magnet).

A83B3F5B726C443482112C7FDE6D3206.description: Describe how the magnetic field of Earth and a magnet are similar.

377FE940378641439F85BF9B5D9CABE8.description: Research and report the use of magnets that is supported by sound scientific principles.

C702499DE8724AA1816131139EF919F9.description: Investigate how magnets will both attract and repel other magnets.

519A1AAC20B64555BF771E64B647E585.description: Compare various types of magnets (e.g., permanent, temporary, and natural magnets) and their abilities to push or pull iron objects they are not touching.

351C923525304B3FB1B2F4864588F622.description: Investigate and compare the behavior of magnetism using magnets.

151BE59AD0FC4737BE432A173F4C3A01.description: Students will understand that magnetism can be observed when there is an interaction between the magnetic fields of magnets or between a magnet and materials made of iron.

65061AD8AC354A529E87EC1A2227C41A.description: Describe and justify how the surface of Earth would appear if there were no mountain uplift, weathering, or erosion.

453D1DE446E74ABC83BBC56C784AEE27.description: Use a time line to identify the sequence and time required for building and breaking down of geologic features on Earth.

0D052CCFD21D49418579A41BE705AC7F.description: Describe the role of deposition in the processes that change Earth's surface.

4827F9CACE1D4817ACE97D8D92555BF0.description: Explain how layers of exposed rock, such as those observed in the Grand Canyon, are the result of natural processes acting over long periods of time.

BBBF0B64B7B74531BFCB3BABBF21E818.description: Relate the building up and breaking down of Earth's surface over time to the various physical land features.

F29C07FC25244052A761B11A1218E205.description: Cite examples of how technology is used to predict volcanoes and earthquakes.

0876A5039E0F4AB9ABAC513D526D2050.description: Describe how volcanoes, earthquakes, and uplift change landforms.

FB9DE05ACF394C53B9533CF684B0F51A.description: Give examples of different landforms that are formed by volcanoes, earthquakes, and uplift (e.g., mountains, valleys, new lakes, canyons).

60E88D93C3AA47EDA5075131D87E1568.description: Identify specific geological features created by volcanoes, earthquakes, and uplift.

1E9F585B5D9E47229ED4EE860205FF04.description: Explain how volcanoes, earthquakes, and uplift affect Earth's surface.

BC06BB392C6349B4818FCEA222FF1E0A.description: Explain the relationship between time and specific geological changes.

220D1C4576F84D5EAACD1B7FDC3E976B.description: Describe how geological features (e.g., valleys, canyons, buttes, arches) are changed through erosion (e.g., waves, wind, glaciers, gravity, running water).

375CBBE0DBA646E58467225C954A5D58.description: Identify the objects, processes, or forces that weather and erode Earth's surface (e.g., ice, plants, animals, abrasion, gravity, water, wind).

688D3CB7CE214A87B83AE9350586B105.description: Describe how weathering and erosion change Earth's surface.

6F7076B2506D4718933A744E912FF7A5.description: Students will understand that volcanoes, earthquakes, uplift, weathering, and erosion reshape Earth's surface.

A2E0E9E68FA94E21A69CC61FB0BC4EA9.description: Hypothesize how changing one of the materials in a chemical reaction will change the results.

E3F218109B6D4C68AB711061212925E4.description: Compare a physical change to a chemical change.

8CA288A3298C404FB22395D2EB94EDF8.description: Cite examples of chemical reactions in daily life.

FC3EFB472092411F8CE67A724B1DB87A.description: Explain why the measured weight of a remaining product is less than its reactants when a gas is produced.

49949E57C64346A9AAFC6AC2056DEA26.description: Identify observable evidence of a chemical reaction (e.g., color change, heat or light given off, heat absorbed, gas given off).

D7AD9B431A464092B3EF394B7E3A9FA8.description: Investigate evidence for changes in matter that occur during a chemical reaction.

06C719C2E0C14EBE9A2B0944E0358554.description: Describe the appearance of a substance before and after a physical change.

C5EBE69BCDAE401F99D7C8F0DA9663ED.description: Compare changes in substances that indicate a physical change has occurred.

5FBC29801C464A5EBA639AADCA0CE462.description: Identify the physical properties of matter (e.g., hard, soft, solid, liquid, gas).

157F4C6293F949F09690ED47F8AD92E2.description: Evaluate evidence that indicates a physical change has occurred.

51A7180311B54DC997D54E3912A27851.description: Investigate chemical reactions in which the total weight of the materials before and after reaction is the same (e.g., cream and vinegar before and after mixing, borax and glue mixed to make a new substance).

B726F16D9FE24BD8B4BBCAB152B72C4F.description: Investigate the results of the combined weights of a liquid and a solid after the solid has been dissolved and then recovered from the liquid (e.g., salt dissolved in water then water evaporated).

1DF6F07DE25B4530A61E33104A7E1831.description: Compare the weight of a specified quantity of matter before and after it undergoes melting or freezing.

31C440392D674156978D61B58CACFDFD.description: Compare the total weight of an object to the weight of its individual parts after being disassembled.

94D8A226015A4961BDED385F5DBDF434.description: Describe that matter is neither created nor destroyed even though it may undergo change.

87DBA720384741F2AD50DDC39B054DE1.description: Students will understand that chemical and physical changes occur in matter.

D2EB5460DFE70131362368A86D17958E.description: Any significant work of art with which the teacher is familiar and appropriately teaches the standards and objectives of this grade level can be used. This could include works suggested for other grade levels as well as other works by the artists suggested above.

D2EB0B40DFE70131362268A86D17958E.description:
Suggested masterworks and artists for third grade:
  • 'Factory Worker' by Mahonri Young
  • 'Channel Three' by Edith Roberson
  • 'Riders of the Range' by Paul Salisbury
  • 'The Cradle' by Berthe Morisot
  • 'My Gems' by William Harnett
  • 'Enamel Saucepan' or other works by Pablo Picasso
  • 'Man in the Golden Helmet' and other works by Rembrandt van Rijn
  • 'La Grande Jatte' by Georges Seurat
  • 'Summertime' by Romare Bearden

D2EAC770DFE70131362168A86D17958E.description: Explore personality or achievements of famous people by examining a significant portrait of them.

D2EA8280DFE70131362068A86D17958E.description: Create a tableau using body shapes invented in dance with elements and principles learned in art.

D2EA3880DFE70131361F68A86D17958E.description: Use a visual arts form as a help in expressing an idea in a nonart subject; e.g., a science project, the writing of a poem, a social studies project.

D2E9DD60DFE70131361E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the connections of visual arts to all learning.

D2E98400DFE70131361D68A86D17958E.description: Describe why a local craft or art form looks like it was made in your area.

D2E93540DFE70131361C68A86D17958E.description: Predict how a work of art or a craft can be connected to an ancient culture.

D2E8F350DFE70131361B68A86D17958E.description: Connect various kinds of art with particular cultures, times, or places.

D2E8ADF0DFE70131361A68A86D17958E.description: Hypothesize why homes and buildings have generally become larger in modern times.

D2E86570DFE70131361968A86D17958E.description: Describe why different cultures may have used different materials to create their arts and crafts.

D2E81C10DFE70131361868A86D17958E.description: Compare the arts of different cultures to explore their similarities and diversities.

D2E7C510DFE70131361768A86D17958E.description: Contextualizing: The student will interpret and apply visual arts in relation to cultures, history, and all learning.

D2E76920DFE70131361668A86D17958E.description: Select some art for public display around the school.

D2E729A0DFE70131361568A86D17958E.description: Create a work of art that uses a similar subject matter, symbol, idea, and/or meaning found in a significant work of art.

D2E6E7C0DFE70131361468A86D17958E.description: Create symbols in art that express individual or group interests.

D2E6A5A0DFE70131361368A86D17958E.description: Judge which works of art most clearly communicate through the use of symbols.

D2E66100DFE70131361268A86D17958E.description: Group significant works of art according to theme or subject matter.

D2E60E20DFE70131361168A86D17958E.description: Discuss, evaluate, and choose symbols, ideas, subject matter, meanings, and purposes for their own artworks.

D2E5CEF0DFE70131361068A86D17958E.description: Describe the difference between crafts and arts; e.g., some crafts have more art in them than other crafts; some crafts are for display and not for practical use. For example, you wouldn't want to cook in some precious ceramic vessels.

D2E59010DFE70131360F68A86D17958E.description: Discuss how an artist's work might be different if it is displayed publicly as opposed to being displayed at home.

D2E55000DFE70131360E68A86D17958E.description: Invent possible stories that may explain what is going on in these same works of art

D2E50C10DFE70131360D68A86D17958E.description: Explain possible meanings or interpretations of some significant works of art.

D2E4BEA0DFE70131360C68A86D17958E.description: Explore possible content and purposes in significant works of art.

D2E46E10DFE70131360B68A86D17958E.description: Expressing: The student will choose and evaluate artistic subject matter, themes, symbols, ideas, meanings, and purposes.

D2E40050DFE70131360A68A86D17958E.description: Create a work of art that uses contrast to create a focal point. Use that to convey the most important idea or part of the work.

D2E3C080DFE70131360968A86D17958E.description: Create a work of art that uses all of the space on the paper.

D2E380C0DFE70131360868A86D17958E.description: Discover how an artist has thoughtfully used all of the space within an artwork.

D2E34290DFE70131360768A86D17958E.description: Group some significant works of art by a common element or visual characteristic.

D2E30370DFE70131360668A86D17958E.description: Identify dominant elements in significant works of art.

D2E2C1B0DFE70131360568A86D17958E.description: Create works of art using the elements and principles.

D2E27A80DFE70131360468A86D17958E.description: Examine significant works of art and point out how the artists have created an illusion or feeling of depth.

D2E215F0DFE70131360368A86D17958E.description: Determine how artists create a dominance in their work; e.g., size, repetition, and contrast.

D2E1D3C0DFE70131360268A86D17958E.description: Analyze and reflect on works of art by their elements and principles.

D2E196A0DFE70131360168A86D17958E.description: Perceiving: The student will analyze, reflect on, and apply the structures of art.

D2E15940DFE70131360068A86D17958E.description: Respect other students ' artworks as well as one's own.

D2E11B60DFE7013135FF68A86D17958E.description: Clean and put back to order art making areas after projects.

D2E0DA50DFE7013135FE68A86D17958E.description: Dispose and/or recycle waste art materials properly.

D2E09390DFE7013135FD68A86D17958E.description: Ventilate the room to avoid inhaling fumes from art materials.

D2E044D0DFE7013135FC68A86D17958E.description: Handle art materials in a safe and responsible manner.

D2E00800DFE7013135FB68A86D17958E.description: Use new art materials and newly learned techniques and processes to celebrate important days and historical events.

D2DFCAE0DFE7013135FA68A86D17958E.description: Use as many art materials as possible to help decorate the room.

D2DF8CF0DFE7013135F968A86D17958E.description: Use a broad range of art materials in supporting the visual arts needs at school.

D2DF4D60DFE7013135F868A86D17958E.description: Explore the design possibilities of a 3-D object by examining views of it from many angles.

D2DF0CA0DFE7013135F768A86D17958E.description: Portray cast shadows as falling opposite their source of light.

D2DEB6E0DFE7013135F668A86D17958E.description: Establish more natural size relationships among objects in drawings.

D2DE5DF0DFE7013135F568A86D17958E.description: Create the appearance of depth by drawing distant objects smaller and with less detail than objects in the foreground.

D2DE1E00DFE7013135F468A86D17958E.description: Make one color dominant in a painting.

D2DD9CD0DFE7013135F268A86D17958E.description: Use simplified forms, such as cones, spheres, and cubes, to begin drawing more complex forms.

D2DD5A60DFE7013135F168A86D17958E.description: Practice using skills for beginning drawings; e.g., blocking-in, stick figures, or drawing the action or gesture of a figure.

D2DD1460DFE7013135F068A86D17958E.description: Explore a variety of art materials while learning new techniques and processes.

D2DCBE80DFE7013135EF68A86D17958E.description: Making: The student will explore and refine the application of media, techniques, and artistic processes.

document.title: Utah Core Standards for Elementary Library Media

14FF72DBA57646C5857AE4C603EF2F9D.description: Students identify issues and consequences of misusing media.

698F1F84923945218B1A26040F9DDCEB.description: Students create, present, and evaluate the final product.

884A58745CAF42C7824AC2C6AAC3E0CF.description: Students develop and apply criteria for quality media productions.

92A5CE9F16C1438086D56FD1D06F2C14.description: Evaluate and select media for personal and educational use.

FF9020E83D3F4FC799AE6323EBA89E16.description: Recognize that media messages are intentionally constructed.

391CAE658FF44C349E1D79D1A22BEB7B.description: Define basic terms and concepts of media.

806FD97567AC4A0C87441769B931E1CF.description: Awareness, modern citizenship, and informed decision making

04095D2010854888853F741C1FD3BC5B.description: Identify areas of personal growth, technology, and time-management skills, including the ability to collaborate.

DA314CE651D44705BE23B8AD9C6FDDAD.description: Reflect upon and describe the level of personal satisfaction with the process and product.

3FA99D5FFCEE4CF08B56C03E66CBBB13.description: Reflect upon how the product could be improved or modified.

843137AD7E7940CDA03C7AD02D1B7CEB.description: Identify areas of the processes that were successfully executed, as well as those needing improvement, to determine how to proceed in the future.

CA219BAF4B724119B70E814982406DF4.description: Solicit, reflect, and act upon peer reviews and teacher comments about the product.

916C92459A9C492490FACBBA686B37FF.description: Reflect upon how the product could be improved or modified.

BB6F8F49A1E64279943C32175CD0F0DE.description: Assess product based on pre-established evaluation criteria.

41026A0AA25C4F08AAD325172A4784D6.description: Evaluate the execution of the product for efficacy and quality, and identify areas need improvement to determine how to proceed in the future.

13976ADB5F3B48218F782C8116AB7081.description: Present a learning product using a variety of presentation techniques (e.g., writing, speaking, media) to communicate new understandings.

92FF44C694ED4633A014D84144FC386F.description: Collaborate with others to exchange ideas, make decisions, create products, and peer edit as appropriate.

A1F5A9B027014D40983F0CC91815D57F.description: Apply evaluation criteria to create, revise, and finalize the learning product.

4F31EBCE541649E190F6C20CAACE5894.description: Follow ethical and legal guidelines in using and citing information to avoid plagiarism and copyright violations.

16A8986650DD4CD8A5A42583CCC37A0C.description: Organize, evaluate, and synthesize selected information to support conclusions.

EEA0DCE7E9DA4BD783ACD4DE442AAE26.description: Monitor gathered information for gaps and weaknesses and modify questions, sources or strategies as needed to elicit adequate information.

2420ABEEBD9F4FFDB5A4FA8D2BF0E09B.description: Use a variety of note-taking strategies, including summarizing and paraphrasing, while noting sources.

E2C1E1287B3E4CB884AF5E7944F0EA4C.description: Validate and compare information in sources, noting differences, contradictions, types of data or research methods.

E7AAEE7F6C4C49AA8EC52BBFDB83D46F.description: Apply critical thinking skills to evaluate and select information in terms of relevancy, currency, and credibility including fact and opinion, bias, prejudice, propaganda.

7AB602D9BBFF46DF8D4D355F55A77D90.description: Analyze and make sense of information (e.g., identifying main ideas, supporting details, bias, point of view, misconceptions, conflicting information).

8153C18E47C14BF382B0E575AF275DD8.description: Use questions to guide reading, listening, and viewing of sources while building connections between prior knowledge and new information.

9FF97F6B61A042F580EEA4F7EC35EF75.description: Engage with information by reading, listening, and viewing sources in a variety of formats.

869BC061D60840BA8F72FDC853B7747B.description: Access information within sources by using relevant tools (e.g., table of contents, indexes, keyword searches, sidebars, related subjects).

D798B7EBD70C417AABABD22BD510167E.description: Revise and focus search as necessary to yield more effective results.

0E97A42F43F9435283A2592A64C63C7F.description: Apply effective location skills, asking for help as needed.

FBD3A2375DBC4AB6A598E7FD1A64E05C.description: Identify information sources (e.g., texts, places, people).

225B54C124E8492EB7122615222CF4A9.description: Generate essential questions for new understanding and to guide inquiry.

9278EDFA86EE44F3BB1B9B4D0A4CFA3E.description: Analyze the task and information needed.

9B5552BF49A44EB08687C4B684BD7760.description: Categorize text as literary or informational.

52EF32337753490BB1631FB886987A56.description: Differentiate between literary (fiction) and informational (non-fiction) text.

40A299017B6E4EF98C587039A0A672B9.description: Listen to, view, read, and integrate information to build a knowledge base.

DD96F9AD4FDC40D58BDD6414A208A4CB.description: Demonstrate perseverance and stamina when reading or listening to a variety of texts.

FA190CB7DCD941C8BB0246A10BE91016.description: Gain understanding and make connections while reading and interacting with text.

4048D1FC223946F197F5170C2A3B649B.description: Select texts from a variety of formats and genres to read for enjoyment, acquire knowledge, and answer questions.

18BF65A474C44ADF914463D33C6831B8.description: Establish reading behaviors for lifelong learning and growth.

66E8FA1F02F9423B928C784034D5DFC6.description: Reading for intellectual, personal, and emotional growth

3B4239EBF6F04B22B08D809026337CB5.description: Explain science concepts and principles using their own words and explanations.

B064951F74194AEF99F7279D4FCB9719.description: Know science information specified for their grade level.

F6DE902253C848178E4E7BF83A7B67F9.description: Pose questions about objects, events, and processes.

F612121E04A64989836EEFE78B8D2A4E.description: Voluntarily read or look at books and other materials about science.

32AB9D46F3354D72B21F675638B876B3.description: Demonstrate a sense of curiosity about nature.

BD75E9EF86A6448A99B794481812D24D.description: Use observations to construct a reasonable explanation.

BDB8314C532740319A45DC569836D4BD.description: Develop and use simple classification systems.

5662341C5D9B43DF8AD833D9516ED169.description: Conduct a simple investigation when given directions.

C8E6AC1CC21A47518B214F2C30CE5289.description: Use instruments to measure length, temperature, volume, and weight using appropriate units.

C46C89B327904A009BB272369287B2E2.description: Make simple predictions and inferences based upon observations.

7007BE2F54054A82BE34EA676D4498B3.description: Sort and sequence data according to a given criterion.

94D7D96B54094D0F9759311AE30EB959.description: Observe simple objects and patterns and report their observations.

A5B2F06ED73043BC867C1E8A71E168B9.description: Use Science Process and Thinking Skills

9EF6A25E1D5C48788D986D7E3EADCFDA.description: Compare relative differences in the amount of heat given off or force required to move an object over lubricated/non-lubricated surfaces and smooth/rough surfaces (e.g., waterslide with and without water, hands rubbing together with and without lotion).

E6C6920B1DEB4A49A8D61565ACB578F7.description: Identify several examples of how rubbing one object against another produces heat.

6BFB1B1D23E942C79B384298DE1D2798.description: Demonstrate that heat may be produced when objects are rubbed against one another.

D0DF764C1ABA4F5496B4698F3884597D.description: Predict, measure, and graph the temperature changes produced by a variety of mechanical machines and electrical devices while they are operating.

0AF497E657A7439C87E73F4B592E75DA.description: List examples of mechanical or electrical devices that produce light.

26A3B8E53954450E8C9C611EE3DB75DA.description: Identify and classify mechanical and electrical sources of heat.

656EE24CC50A4C7AA6528F258E7B1615.description: Demonstrate that mechanical and electrical machines produce heat and sometimes light.

C118CC33A00644CF8F50ECBE87119DF5.description: Identify and discuss as a class some misconceptions about heat sources (e.g., clothes do not produce heat, ice cubes do not give off cold).

7D51FF21BC65444AB0F88222F9545E7D.description: Provide examples of how sunlight affects people and animals by providing heat and light.

A26512C8655848FC8FAFF6C3D5AF4BEB.description: Observe and report how sunlight affects plant growth.

C89739EBDDA54EC496D882670AABE17E.description: Compare temperatures in sunny and shady places.

82FBE1FCB9FD477AA50E2EBB4528DF95.description: Provide evidence showing that the sun is the source of heat and light for Earth.

6E659B77E1F9474F88FA18CF058B2C0E.description: Students will understand that the sun is the main source of heat and light for things living on Earth. They will also understand that the motion of rubbing objects together may produce heat.

CCE3E3F47A5545F3BEEBCFD7A7E9771E.description: Pose questions about gravity and forces.

FC7848E3059D4C3A8B57BAF4013742FC.description: Observe, record, and compare the effect of gravity on several objects in motion (e.g., a thrown ball and a dropped ball falling to Earth).

D98D72C286CA4D9695983F32EBAFDA3D.description: Compare how the motion of an object rolling up or down a hill changes with the incline of the hill.

FB16AA2F18434C11A06E7569D9C4F98A.description: Describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object.

90138F40BE6748BB94D309FA72E4C4CD.description: Use measurement to demonstrate that heavier objects require more force than lighter ones to overcome gravity.

217DC9ADBAF34A41A08BD342A7A95A48.description: Demonstrate that a force is required to overcome gravity.

D374465E31AD4591AA4FB00717DDE04D.description: Demonstrate that gravity is a force.

E03CD0784A7F4C74AFA279F1C42180C3.description: Students will understand that objects near Earth are pulled toward Earth by gravity.

D0C704A0E4B34D3E8215010C0356856D.description: Show how these concepts apply to various activities (e.g., batting a ball, kicking a ball, hitting a golf ball with a golf club) in terms of force, motion, speed, direction, and distance (e.g. slow, fast, hit hard, hit soft).

1C8B76B56A97486AB3F56246469E2177.description: Conduct a simple investigation to show what happens when objects of various weights collide with one another (e.g., marbles, balls).

66C6B9FFF34F41D194E79A333CD1EB7F.description: Compare the relative effects of forces of different strengths on an object (e.g., strong wind affects an object differently than a breeze).

7DF53881B4D84437883E75E2DD47C1C3.description: Compare and chart the relative effects of a force of the same strength on objects of different weight (e.g., the breeze from a fan will move a piece of paper but may not move a piece of cardboard).

AD71BA920C70428B912E90D80B1FCE81.description: Predict and observe what happens when a force is applied to an object (e.g., wind, flowing water).

4A181D2CF6EB4D2F96782B56417262FA.description: Demonstrate that the greater the force applied to an object, the greater the change in speed or direction of the object.

87D94091950645C4894F8F8C01EBAAA8.description: Investigate how forces applied through simple machines affect the direction and/or amount of resulting force.

1D9BD70350104847883FD2FEF977B38E.description: Compare the forces of pushing and pulling.

407A4C11D7D4425F81A346575B930558.description: Show that objects at rest will not move unless a force is applied to them.

42943EA75EDE4C4987A09609E5B7D186.description: Demonstrate how forces cause changes in speed or direction of objects.

9B17F77CE93440F2896452023FF1C107.description: Students will understand the relationship between the force applied to an object and resulting motion of the object.

DED2AAEE2E5848538C4BC64514017E59.description: Pose a question about the interaction between living and nonliving things in the environment that could be investigated by observation.

5BE53CFD925F4B03BE4E2168C8F6098E.description: Compare a small-scale environment to a larger environment (e.g., aquarium to a pond, terrarium to a forest).

7DDEB81E5CB64C48A53426ECA14DF361.description: Observe and record the effect of changes (e.g., temperature, amount of water, light) upon the living organisms and nonliving things in a small-scale environment.

1201A1A1A0F34EBFB656BD8C43E0937C.description: Predict the effects of changes in the environment (e.g., temperature, light, moisture) on a living organism.

3831A61DC6344ACB9D826ABB7439E2C9.description: Identify living and nonliving things in a small environment (e.g., terrarium, aquarium, flowerbed) composed of living and nonliving things.

9A91C8E7277B4E49AE88F38E34F6A4A4.description: Describe the interactions between living and nonliving things in a small environment.

DD9E0C10DC894A6A821113B456855A28.description: Classify living and nonliving things in an environment.

35D7A71698264B909798277F5AB4368B.description: Identify characteristics of living things (i.e., growth, movement, reproduction).

D98F56BC37E64FC2BA7E755072C97789.description: Classify living and nonliving things in an environment.

95F71F86FF2547F495B2B4CE89C0F418.description: Students will understand that organisms depend on living and nonliving things within their environment.

0DCBCCF1B49F4DBEAE2A719C2E56DC8A.description: Use a model to demonstrate why it seems to a person on Earth that the sun, planets, and stars appear to move across the sky.

CE8DED0DCC344FD992394FC75D5FC2C1.description: Use a model of Earth to demonstrate that Earth rotates on its axis once every 24 hours to produce the night and day cycle.

322AE05D41754903AF8403D229A2BD11.description: Use a chart to show that the moon orbits Earth approximately every 28 days.

F933C1625B2B44A2B50AC04AFA4BB3A2.description: Describe the motions of Earth (i.e., the rotation [spinning] of Earth on its axis, the revolution [orbit] of Earth around the sun).

E5200D5ACBF04E6086E17A1D2D498632.description: Describe the movement of Earth and the moon and the apparent movement of other bodies through the sky.

CDC988FDB9004A1D92A31AD7AAF5C2EE.description: List the differences in the physical appearance of Earth and the moon as viewed from space.

DD65D96472784EC6B15E8C444E89109A.description: Explain that the sun is the source of light that lights the moon.

88B1D63707B74ED5AD9E0CC1537BEAA9.description: Describe the shape of Earth and the moon as spherical.

C9D024A6CC194F3A8DCFB8879D6A2064.description: Describe the appearance of Earth and the moon.

FAB00322DEFB4C64890414F351EB08DB.description: Students will understand that the shape of Earth and the moon are spherical and that Earth rotates on its axis to produce the appearance of the sun and moon moving through the sky.
