46DF1487EE1F4E0C985AEF40937F2B3D.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Note the effect of multiple transformations on a single function and the common effect of each transformation across function types. Include functions defined only by a graph. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

9E173783A6D14ADDB9AAE5FDF1CA3B0D.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
comments: For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

D08AAE3E2B7547089F09EFCA4AC4732B.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).
comments: For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.

1925B2EC41C14E318A0119051CE654E5.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

4AA13284A6A949C0B55FD27A71C0F044.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior; and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

E4FA55B729AF444881D33CAF8CE1763B.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions. Compare and contrast square root, cubed root, and step functions with all other functions.

155F0DDC4A30445EA43C9A59502166D0.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

126C82FB051A47ABA7DF697E85D23D4F.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

84E0B2C34BB34658B40736F82CC3C878.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.
comments: For example, if the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.

5CD5C3A668104EA599B1B1AC9377968C.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship.
comments: Key features include intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

B5B995BD41604EA5B4E98DCA7544A96F.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, for example, using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

6BEF99B966C0403CA3BA05D87BA1D0F9.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

F4DC080000504EFD8B3C26A7FA5D4A6D.description: Algebra: Reasoning With Equations and Inequalities

ED7042AAC129448484AFB0C74058629D.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.
comments: For example, rearrange the compound interest formula to solve for t: A = P(1+ r/n)<sup>nt</sup>

83202120E28B4DE5BE218E16A528C042.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options ina modeling context.
comments: For example, maximizing the volume of a box for a given surface area while drawing attention to the practical domain.

E32F0813FED84D57BE5A785DEE950B6F.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

585AB94FBE2A4C25A1A20EA22272FADF.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

50034545E60B4F5BB290B20A5E00AE94.description: Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

2951B849FE804706B2F359D73BC5CC89.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

1C3C4FF2E2D94C25AA0547514062C3F1.description: Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)<sup>n</sup> in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers.
comments: For example, with coefficients determined by Pascal's Triangle.

2E625B3AA7344C47BDBE34E4086D960F.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.
comments: For example, the polynomial identity (x² + y²)² = (x² – y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

1DD1274F48CE4EB9A3825E906322C734.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

046D89C9D81C4B17AB0F35C86B42BAF6.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x – a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

D34E0F6C45C44D5DAF2C3655306E62EA.description: Understand that all polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

FF57D09E5CDE4E4FBF6ACE571531519E.description: Algebra — Arithmetic With Polynomials and Rational Expressions

F662307D6F0B4E2C98B64A046EBAA667.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a geometric series, and use the formula to solve problems. Extend to infinite geometric series.
comments: For example, calculate mortgage payments.

2347050D5C934308B6E8D8CABF74D4A8.description: Derive the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series.

16D2DCCE0791422780B2CCA86B2986DD.description: Understand the formula for the sum of a series and use the formula to solve problems.

76B41FCD28334E0DBE22999B7FD1934F.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.
comments: For example, see x<sup>4</sup> – y<sup>4</sup> as (x²)² – (y²)², thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x² – y²)(x² + y²).

D6F20CC226E24EE8A6FBCBF61D3E04E8.description: Interpret complex expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
comments: For example, examine the behavior of P(1+r/n)<sup>nt</sup> as n becomes large.

B6E18B80066449F5AA92ED13DEC1498B.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

A721ECB4BCC347928521EC731AFD451C.description: Interpret polynomial and rational expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

9EA076121F384489955A34017441C19B.description: Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials. Limit to polynomials with real coefficients.

C7A0B5C80D354CFBA039E37C051835CD.description: Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.
comments: For example, rewrite x² + 4 as (x + 2i)(x – 2i).

C2608404C1B24A4D9B2BBD61EBD3552F.description: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System

5CFDE02E1942495E84E019709EC465C4.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning. Notice if reasoning is repeated, and look for both generalizations and shortcuts. Evaluate the reasonableness of intermediate results by maintaining oversight of the process while attending to the details.

FDE3E3E856B543F282E8581DD8AE9C04.description: Look for and make use of structure. Look closely at mathematical relationships to identify the underlying structure by recognizing a simple structure within a more complicated structure. See complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects.
comments: For example, see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

5F5057F782A74576A1C3B0CCB5A21465.description: Attend to precision. Communicate precisely to others. Use explicit definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose. Specify units of measure and label axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. Calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context.

F6EDDFB3FEA542D2B70C19FB80C43345.description: Use appropriate tools strategically. Consider the available tools and be sufficiently familiar with them to make sound decisions about when each tool might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained as well as the limitations. Identify relevant external mathematical resources and use them to pose or solve problems. Use tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

AD494664C46D4F73A43ACEDC64AB03B5.description: Model with mathematics. Apply mathematics to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. Make assumptions and approximations, identifying important quantities to construct a mathematical model. Routinely interpret mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

3B091A3306354CA4B179E55E5A356024.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others. Understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. Make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. Justify conclusions and communicate them to others. Respond to the arguments of others by listening, asking clarifying questions, and critiquing the reasoning of others.

B1888EAC13DB4579815BEDBE4C405E98.description: Reason abstractly and quantitatively. Make sense of the quantities and their relationships in problem situations. Translate between context and algebraic representations by contextualizing and decontextualizing quantitative relationships. This includes the ability to decontextualize a given situation, representing it algebraically and manipulating symbols fluently as well as the ability to contextualize algebraic representations to make sense of the problem.

837F027B96A54BF099EEA93D41EAF0F7.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them. Explain the meaning of a problem and look for entry points to its solution. Analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. Make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution, plan a solution pathway, and continually monitor progress asking, "Does this make sense?" Consider analogous problems, make connections between multiple representations, identify the correspondence between different approaches, look for trends, and transform algebraic expressions to highlight meaningful mathematics. Check answers to problems using a different method.

FF3C1D1E2D09472BBADD7B5BD0C7D455.description: Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

315003CC364D423581B40215D4A9D412.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

20D3711892E049AAB1D3A96C0345C59D.description: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

D2F17C9A6173463396D99CD6925FCC48.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

FFFEA433550E40879CC5A11A1A92676B.description: Statistics and Probability — Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

F7D743331B694B6886EB0F384AC2D5A6.description: Derive the equations of ellipses and hyperbolas given the foci, using the fact that the sum or difference of distances from the foci is constant.

06B04AC72FB24A898963281AAF22492B.description: Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix.

32DDA15C51DF4F8C928DA1A036B68096.description: Geometry — Expressing Geometric Properties With Equations

FEFCC9AD6BB8479B8E8C88EBF15AFDA3.description: Represent series algebraically, graphically, and numerically.

B4CC771AE1EF4976B4867A14329D84ED.description: Use sigma notation to represent the sum of a finite arithmetic or geometric series.

0E265D2D1ED249AFB6ED5E8FF8C34497.description: Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists, and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).

B2A5A9F4F82240679CA1F3FC8E939C5F.description: Represent a system of linear equations as a single-matrix equation in a vector variable.

9CCED67C61344ECBA93C8BD0D2D06B01.description: Algebra — Reasoning With Equations and Inequalities

0EBF6B0C2CC74FED8E4695C2CD943D42.description: Represent addition, subtraction, and multiplication geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation.
comments: For example, (-1 + √3i)3 = 8 because (-1 + √3i) has modulus 2 and argument 120°.

D949DE3151794A81926CA166112CE909.description: Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular form, and explain why the rectangular form of a given complex number represents the same number.

32D8F47E3E7A481A82898870111CF5AC.description: Find the conjugate of a complex number; use conjugates to find moduli and quotients of complex numbers.

837CF1AC3EFC4800BD4782813542EB65.description: Number and Quantity — Complex Number System

7D0EC34A1E5C4AA8A0EC73B9806A4507.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

55951B81D1FA4508B0226C1C33E63882.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.
comments: For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if you are are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung cancer.

1300D4511E474A9FAC0478421DF8096C.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.
comments: For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their favorite subject among math, science, and English. Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other subjects and compare the results.

83992E6DD0324C6883293694C985DC70.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

3B53C59FF8FF4CB0A7B244226F310EB6.description: Statistics — Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

5BB08791423043D884E86BB2D108E56D.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and condition reltive frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the date.

0270A94A8CC84AE98DD5ADEF31F4C165.description: Statistics — Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data

6E2B5B6CF5614EB59EFDBEE1A20339BF.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems. Informal arguments for volume formulas can make use of the way in which volume scale under similarity transformations: when one figure results from another by applying a similarity transformation, volumes of solid figures scale by k³ under a similarity transformation with scale factor k.

764F4287E2D94D449CADB110D1350F72.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Informal arguments for area formulas can make use of the way in which area scale under similarity transformations: when one figure in the plane results from another by applying a similarity transformation with scale factor k, its area is k² times the area of the first.
comments: Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri's principle, and informal limit arguments.

BF11CE74349742D1ADF10A5BC3056642.description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

2F8240C9EB4843E9AECF3C41A6F36E3E.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.
comments: For example, prove or disprove that a figure defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle; prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle centered at the origin and containing the point (0, 2).

8818B97CBC66488DB3B7433DD3CFE0AB.description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

786F12391ED64A978268548E381F1410.description: Geometry — Expressing Geometric Properties With Equations

F4E85C611675443381C7340727BAEDA8.description: Derive, using similarity, the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

1108B589A11C481481F9CCDC563563BF.description: Construct a tangent line from a point outside a given circle to the circle.

E1E03207FED24C53BED6CFF9948AD16E.description: Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

20DB2C8A68C843E6BF4A6717A76357FD.description: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords.
comments: Relationships include the relationship between central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a diameter are right angles; the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the radius intersects the circle.

85320CA28C2C4251BB5EC72CBFED9A42.description: Prove that all circles are similar.

A5B94029C3074138A32BFDDC56555694.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

FD79BA7A059A46AAA8C3639DAE1B3B0E.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

A23EFD982B2C44E1B9DDEAC94616ECC9.description: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

ED8D60B540CE45389750B14C4F9E63EC.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

comments: Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two proportionally and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem (proved using triangle similarity).

4448DA2AB9C3491D85B27FCD65D2AE73.description: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar.

C72E27E7695D4977A97F65E84149A203.description: Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide whether they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides.

643E538F36E5472F8998FF96A20B8080.description: The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale factor.

478000D72D5D4365B5368B5E0C0099C4.description: A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.

152B9A7615E14E46B42E2420DBA36292.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor.

9E8BDAD8364F4ED6A45AFD929E879F49.description: Geometry — Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry

comments: Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent, opposite angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely, rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals.

Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.

445A6F05B8BD4396B0C65774CD2761D0.description: Prove theorems about lines and angles.
comments: Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment's endpoints.

BAC9DA15B9E746CDA5D9AA94BAB71114.description: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ), given sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ), and the quadrant of the angle.

5F65B5F4C9A84BEDAE465637ABB6A8BD.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function. Compare linear and exponential growth to quadratic growth.

CC0C5FF401BE425480CC1ACEE4C3EAC2.description: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models

57D2B2B825DF45B4AB42F1FEDB9E392A.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Focus on quadratic functions and consider including absolute value functions. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

F80D32EC622C4FA4ABEAD429CBEE7674.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
comments: For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

D219CBB197284D19BC0D552EFE728E83.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

3CA81B3F8D03472689BA0AFDBBBC74D1.description: Write a quadratic or exponential function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

4D44E99ECF364462A1FC6DDCB09B38D8.description: Compare properties of two functions, each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). Extend work with quadratics to include the relationship between coefficients and roots, and that once roots are known, a quadratic equation can be factored.
comments: For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.

93586FC303F44BE68E8C3764D39D582F.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example, identify percent rate of change in functions such as y = (1.02)<sup>t</sup>, y = (0.97)<sup>t</sup>, y = (1.01)<sup>12t</sup>, y = (1.2)<sup>t/10</sup>, and classify them as representing exponential growth or decay.

3897690DDC9042DE925B044A825ED07F.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

F6D0E84865C5470AAA4C3B955E56E3AD.description: Write a function defined by an expression in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

AFF70F22B3D14759AE42A637C3253DAC.description: Graph piecewise-defined functions and absolute value functions. Compare and contrast absolute value and piecewise-defined functions with linear, quadratic, and exponential functions. Highlight issues of domain, range, and usefulness when examining piecewise-defined functions.

D1FE9060A6F740A5858348E3B2BD2863.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

D679635A77D34B3AA6F4B5F3055504A7.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

1CD7573F48214688939A08A08CABA571.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

39C140CBA75046D3A54D4198385BBF73.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. Focus on quadratic functions; compare with linear and exponential functions.
comments: For example, if the function h(n) gives the number of personhours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.

00F4C3343682446DB9035DBB13C8A2E5.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship.
comments: Key features include intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

79EA95DF076C4DE68B91BDEC7D36F481.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.
comments: For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = –3x and the circle x² + y² = 3.

31CA07C041B8482B9AB91F2CB9D64B87.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

9253139EFDC54A4DB510F6BE299F896C.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

ADEFEB54B5254F41BE9EBD799DC1F872.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

C52D4D0D29AD4FE98A3FC4483AB8FC0B.description: Algebra — Reasoning With Equations and Inequalities

76E19232755545F1A970521573EBF9BC.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations; extend to formulas involving squared variables.
comments: For example, rearrange the formula for the volume of a cylinder V = πr² h.

3A87DE1F9AE44158A31DB8B4A27CDB56.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

28A8D1E4F45649C694DF832C16067029.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

48553801B50646B58A947F749ABEB9EE.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

2F86CB849AC44EDD9A563D59F8E8515E.description: Algebra — Arithmetic With Polynomials and Rational Expressions

2F809545ACCA4CEFBD7ED025A9E04649.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example, the expression 1.15<sup>t</sup> can be rewritten as (1.15<sup>1/12</sup>)<sup>12t</sup> ≈ 1.012<sup>12t</sup> to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

4A5D8D2556D446059ACDDF145F9F92F7.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

74CBA46B2E4C4D4AA54C0A8D0FFA9D24.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

0DB3C4F304C646F195D00C4C1ECD426E.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.
comments: For example, development of skill in factoring and completing the square goes hand in hand with understanding what different forms of a quadratic expression reveal.

1C7B3CD0273D46B3BBBC17671E48C906.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.
comments: For example, see x<sup>4</sup> – y<sup>4</sup> as (x²)² – (y²)², thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x² – y²)(x² + y²).

6286B814D8164485BCE1400A29E9DC9D.description: Interpret increasingly more complex expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. Exponents are extended from the integer exponents to rational exponents focusing on those that represent square or cube roots.

6357772C752445FBA31CCE9DA9637073.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

9A77EB5F9E0C42EBAD7A160BC1C11345.description: Interpret quadratic and exponential expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

9BFEF13191B74B208C86204E3EA7769A.description: Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

5D4DEA3BBE2941E5A4F4E3E7CC01A7E0.description: Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers. Limit to quadratics with real coefficients.
comments: For example, rewrite x² + 4 as (x + 2i)(x – 2i).

F2F96FB4478749D7A9A48F86F63F4540.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

56E3BC748CFD43B0804A19534F1095C3.description: Use the relation i² = -1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers. Limit to multiplications that involve i² as the highest power of i.

04D0DAA6CA0E4F78BB9833D226ABCED8.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = -1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real.

4BA1E5FCC4CB46D294928B6C9CE7D233.description: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System

DC82401CDC09498483A37D624E99FB3D.description: Explain why sums and products of rational numbers are rational, that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational, and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational. Connect to physical situations (e.g., finding the perimeter of a square of area 2).

479D760DB60B43988CA5B0BBF1D92CD8.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

ED027DC7BF7A45B1B20308543E5ABE74.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.
comments: For example, we define 5<sup>1/3</sup> to be the cube root of 5 because we want (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ = 5(<sup>1/3</sup>)³ to hold, so (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ must equal 5.

3403EEE644234A71A6FE7DD47DBCC044.description: Number and Quantity — The Real Number System

8AD7B01355414490B25D0C8871CC751E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning. Notice if reasoning is repeated, and look for both generalizations and shortcuts. Evaluate the reasonableness of intermediate results by maintaining oversight of the process while attending to the details.

CBB722EEA2104BAC9EE98BA6A30C6414.description: Look for and make use of structure. Look closely at mathematical relationships to identify the underlying structure by recognizing a simple structure within a more complicated structure. See complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects.
comments: For example, see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

6EE4BFB4DFE940539DF8251C18E72EAB.description: Attend to precision. Communicate precisely to others. Use explicit definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose. Specify units of measure and label axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. Calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context.

67EA51293ADC4BDAA216E1DAB532F10B.description: Use appropriate tools strategically. Consider the available tools and be sufficiently familiar with them to make sound decisions about when each tool might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained as well as the limitations. Identify relevant external mathematical resources and use them to pose or solve problems. Use tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

7849FB57583D4F5D82A10DE5222FBFF6.description: Model with mathematics. Apply mathematics to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. Make assumptions and approximations, identifying important quantities to construct a mathematical model. Routinely interpret mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

8A3059A2212F4F53B11BED189A4D04FC.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others. Understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. Make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. Justify conclusions and communicate them to others. Respond to the arguments of others by listening, asking clarifying questions, and critiquing the reasoning of others.

281B7214753C4CA0A44E2B3AEFE6B35D.description: Reason abstractly and quantitatively. Make sense of the quantities and their relationships in problem situations. Translate between context and algebraic representations by contextualizing and decontextualizing quantitative relationships. This includes the ability to decontextualize a given situation, representing it algebraically and manipulating symbols fluently as well as the ability to contextualize algebraic representations to make sense of the problem.

807F4BE37FC14508AE6C361B87A57A19.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them. Explain the meaning of a problem and look for entry points to its solution. Analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. Make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution, plan a solution pathway, and continually monitor progress asking, "Does this make sense?" Consider analogous problems, make connections between multiple representations, identify the correspondence between different approaches, look for trends, and transform algebraic expressions to highlight meaningful mathematics. Check answers to problems using a different method.

90FF7ED037F044ADA36E351EBE6AAB90.description: Solve systems of linear equations up to three variables using matrix row reduction.

EB369A9643E24AB48F578461F70B7449.description: Work with 2 × 2 matrices as transformations of the plane, and interpret the absolute value of the determinant in terms of area.

1679C1D26C384E8FAC2B5C4A28F90443.description: Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors.

579271576762409791E140E4A2ABF751.description: Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

5A98DF7FB6134641A911FDAB0DB19575.description: Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.

7B8619A9EFA64FA49E6C63DF81D6D01A.description: Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions.

5BD0723E6B97490693A3D8D506B426CD.description: Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices, e.g., as when all of the pay-offs in a game are doubled.

56DC4242CC824F38BDD5085FEFC7D847.description: Use matrices to represent and manipulate data, e.g., to represent payoffs or incidence relationships in a network.

FDBD2AC6158A4E68B77953EDECD7A120.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ≠ 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against vs (for c < 0).

BFC6454147044627B85FD1AD21BA247B.description: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction; perform scalar multiplication component-wise, e.g., as c(vx , vy) = (cvx , cvy).

A789F8D9794D4D08B87340333E8DF3A5.description: Multiply a vector by a scalar.

7D0C74EB793E4102AA1CE621935840F4.description: Understand vector subtraction v – w as v + (–w), where –w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector subtraction component-wise.

1160EE4213D34C56AAB9BEA448E07DBD.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.

38F9DB9E5EBF4B19A409408D5F255FDC.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule. Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.

3239C478538449CEA9CB6107264544A3.description: Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors.

9762CC76F0BC4B09902D501A6BBC50DE.description: Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

DC19C4690923420FA2DFF3651B66C40A.description: Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).

E17614335B8A476EA8376D9ED0CAF143.description: Number and Quantity: Vector and Matrix Quantities

052F9DE192DA4D62AD52BCF70C72FED2.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

241A25A98CDD49FEBE36F1FD53960C2C.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

46BBB12E00864C9A9B774AE923B35F4B.description: Fit a linear function for scatter plots that suggest a linear association.

8EDDA585C07F48FFB8EA47C7228C849E.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals. Focus on situations for which linear models are appropriate.

CB923C336C4F4C34A67CEBBE2065717A.description: Fit a linear function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions, or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear and exponential models.

A976B93E3BAC4DB6B495E5DE9F3446F6.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

743DC9840B74485C97A5549469A1230C.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers). Calculate the weighted average of a distribution and interpret it as a measure of center.

6DE16D7091394F999B733EFCE771514E.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

B2250555BAE647CA966A7E5CB0945441.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

4044F3BA43474852B357631179EB08C7.description: Statistics and Probability — Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data

920043091C854F6082D5B0F6F76EC38D.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles; e.g., connect with The Pythagorean Theorem and the distance formula.

72C42FFE8D9E4E3195A69EB61AB5698C.description: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines; use them to solve geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point).

42994B2F66554673BC61B64A2A08A19D.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.
comments: For example, prove or disprove that a figure defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle; prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle centered at the origin and containing the point (0, 2).

BFDFC0860D3C41258D09703DBAC3BEDF.description: Geometry — Expressing Geometric Properties With Equations

015F2BD2DECB43A8A0EA1B3D156B089C.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle. Emphasize the ability to formalize and defend how these constructions result in the desired objects.

AB4F72E01691453BA440DEDC9176A46D.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.). Emphasize the ability to formalize and defend how these constructions result in the desired objects.
comments: For example, copying a segment; copying an angle; bisecting a segment; bisecting an angle; constructing perpendicular lines, including the perpendicular bisector of a line segment; and constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point not on the line.

5938F4E1D7A841359F0DD6297AB19D4C.description: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.

DCAC9C599B154BFD9CD8726CF2DAC221.description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

04D38F9CFB5146288A6CA113F431CBE1.description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide whether they are congruent.

5E8A056F52CA4B9F9A5755F5DA93D90F.description: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, for example, graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another. Point out the basis of rigid motions in geometric concepts, for example, translations move points a specified distance along a line parallel to a specified line; rotations move objects along a circular arc with a specified center through a specified angle.

F18308C710924217B52C5A7BF647EA67.description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

4D51D7AD54584BD2864892B1AA8F0FA7.description: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.

88A6269EA10148C897BEF5AAD16BF2F0.description: Represent transformations in the plane using, for example, transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).

3731748414A64810ABCC7D5419FDD591.description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

14E8888B2652408F94F79207A159E298.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context. Limit exponential functions to those of the form f(x) = b<sup>x</sup> + k.

CD92F6B6D62C4A398D7BAD0946F55168.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly.

B604037B68654D22B0BD48E892DDF688.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

02DAD33889224198B62A07A245EA36E4.description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

5E7D9D08A56545788E7E1BBB51F1869A.description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

156E55A0806F40829D8BAFC952FEAB66.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals; exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

D13318E4C5FF47409304DA0AF865E95A.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

34DAB76DA5B64014AD7E48EA438B46E1.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Relate the vertical translation of a linear function to its y-intercept. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology.

A1BB8862EDCF448FB9F89A8476984C59.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms. Limit F.BF.1a, 1b, and 2 to linear and exponential functions. Connect arithmetic sequences to linear functions and geometric sequences to exponential functions.

6F169BE74F3D4F039FC992104466A6E9.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
comments: For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

C3EA99B29E2C49C0B67110F916BF5E94.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

9F4571D8B1FB487F9DCCEA694B6D3186.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

F0BDA36E2E314D34ABD597D04A9B053F.description: Functions — Building Linear or Exponential Functions

74C8EBF3CD5B447A8749EA5FCEBCD081.description: Compare properties of two functions, each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).
comments: For example, compare the growth of two linear functions, or two exponential functions such as y=3<sup>n</sup> and y=100•2<sup>n</sup>.

098CBC9D6FCC4D96BF5BB030E75D885D.description: Graph exponential functions, showing intercepts and end behavior.

63868ECD0BB2416493146501FAD05195.description: Graph linear functions and show intercepts.

6648EA4E442C424ABB3C7F622EB24DEF.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

195D92AD06C242BFBCE83282C6252D81.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

5D2407491EE04D4E965E0FAFF6B70F54.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.
comments: For example, if the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.

B12496375EB44CF8A7A2148BEC79CDAF.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; and end behavior.

B7783832B315427D902C1086A0DB1E20.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers. Recognize arithmetic and geometric sequences as examples of linear and exponential functions.
comments: For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n+1) = f(n) + f(n-1) for n ≥ 1.

4A6284C24B1C4CDFB55F576D1E488711.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

CC5B25C348AB4E4C90367FCE34F58BEA.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

D67C20E9FC4343ACB4F827CC1FAF7B82.description: Functions — Interpreting Linear and Exponential Functions

8799932D0B274CFBAD08856E1430ABC3.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a halfplane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

581323F90CE34214AD865EEB007A1E7A.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately; e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear and exponential functions.

85D7E9A81AE14DE39325432F1CCD2C7B.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

8D616A6CFF5C41858CB4EF9D8C88D013.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (numerically, algebraically, graphically), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

2CF7DAA7C1C441D5BF9CFE60BA5AAD36.description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

5A383DA1DE924621A03307F63A41F79F.description: Solve simple exponential equations that rely only on application of the laws of exponents (limit solving exponential equations to those that can be solved without logarithms).
comments: For example, 5<sup>x</sup> = 125 or 2<sup>x</sup> = 1/16.

3315EDBBD8994A1E81FCB5D7CEFA94EB.description: Solve compound inequalities in one variable, including absolute value inequalities.

EDCE101D1888416F91C8405B1CF3AED1.description: Solve one-variable equations and literal equations to highlight a variable of interest.

342F3DC3E465425EA374BF06494C38AA.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

FE4F1C6AA7674560B319D3EB65A9ECE1.description: Explain each step in solving a linear equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method. Students will solve exponential equations with logarithms in Secondary Mathematics III.

8B38BEA7473747E9BAA155892A53D395.description: Algebra — Reasoning With Equations and Inequalities

ABE637CDACB84C4E85FA311D01B3A67E.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.
comments: For example, rearrange Ohm's Law V = IR to highlight resistance R.

5A455155ED90403A94D054221EBDEBEA.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.
comments: For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.

CEE6C672C3A941C8B0892D1D3EA748A0.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

C8BD734937CF44379A337526A47FC311.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and simple exponential functions.

4DBBD7E8320646C5831FDE1FE21A090C.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
comments: For example, interpret P(1 + r)<sup>n</sup> as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

01B4D2DC91654EFCBCD5ACC3CC64320A.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

95914CDBBFAE4CFEB359497CC4E0AB3C.description: Interpret linear expressions and exponential expressions with integer exponents that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

2615FE39394F4F979C23981E4C175E67.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

0278E6C1C2B94D95905D76D11D8CB0DB.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

4F6924383EDC470C92A60ECF4B8B9AC1.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

09F6FA031DB14E6296E9FD530BDC8185.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning. Notice if reasoning is repeated, and look for both generalizations and shortcuts. Evaluate the reasonableness of intermediate results by maintaining oversight of the process while attending to the details.

2FAB688CD99F4E5B8474E71A6C16D77F.description: Look for and make use of structure. Look closely at mathematical relationships to identify the underlying structure by recognizing a simple structure within a more complicated structure. See complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects.
comments: For example, see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

7BE2C04362884022A675A9286CC830D0.description: Attend to precision. Communicate precisely to others. Use explicit definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose. Specify units of measure and label axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. Calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context.

EAC42818A31F4032A61C6E064B8D1B3E.description: Use appropriate tools strategically. Consider the available tools and be sufficiently familiar with them to make sound decisions about when each tool might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained as well as the limitations. Identify relevant external mathematical resources and use them to pose or solve problems. Use tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

6FFA640A33B84E7DBE17C00F424EC569.description: Model with mathematics. Apply mathematics to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. Make assumptions and approximations, identifying important quantities to construct a mathematical model. Routinely interpret mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

B5D1667A3B6B4F309428E756D7136162.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others. Understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. Make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. Justify conclusions and communicate them to others. Respond to the arguments of others by listening, asking clarifying questions, and critiquing the reasoning of others.

8AB6328014C14D54B4C4769C97CB5512.description: Reason abstractly and quantitatively. Make sense of the quantities and their relationships in problem situations. Translate between context and algebraic representations by contextualizing and decontextualizing quantitative relationships. This includes the ability to decontextualize a given situation, representing it algebraically and manipulating symbols fluently as well as the ability to contextualize algebraic representations to make sense of the problem.

0DD2EA83453A4B949C137AED76D57D38.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them. Explain the meaning of a problem and look for entry points to its solution. Analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. Make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution, plan a solution pathway, and continually monitor progress asking, "Does this make sense?" Consider analogous problems, make connections between multiple representations, identify the correspondence between different approaches, look for trends, and transform algebraic expressions to highlight meaningful mathematics. Check answers to problems using a different method.

document.title: Utah Core Standards for Physical Education

8FA2590893CA41F6A9C702ECAAF59C76.description: Describe the positive social interactions that result from participation in physical activity.

1F533A4CC8B44B03BFB9957539367366.description: Discuss the challenge that comes from learning a new physical activity.

73FF8797545245C1A8D43AA83ECA3F55.description: Reflect on the personal selection of particular physical activities over other options.

3BFFD4C63DDF44979A07705C5455F7CE.description: Discuss the relationship between physical activity and good health.

397B1DC518CB454DA3C26D6A62815007.description: Students will appraise the personal value of physical activity as a tool for wellness, challenges, and interacting with appropriate social skills with friends and family.

03D7DC97DB7342C8B077E37CEB3A8126.description: Demonstrate understanding of safety, rules, and etiquette by working safely and cooperatively in physical activity.

68A87F811A21419DB45A19811491D23B.description: Exhibit etiquette and adherence to rules in a variety of physical activities.

B81B6046353145C4A36BBB7898FA6994.description: Recognize others' success in movement performance.

F79675FD66D34F16B20F487DB56A7D48.description: Respond appropriately to suggestions given by teacher.

EE69F21C364948709EE185BA21D0AA86.description: Work independently for extended periods of time.

D8F1FCC26FD7429CB328AF6CB62D18B0.description: Exhibit personal responsibility in teacher-directed activities.

DD456C894EFF4370BBC2E7583879EE4F.description: Students will develop cooperative skills and positive personal behavior through communication and respect for self and others.

A330DEC627034F65871E5EAC41356CA8.description: Understand the importance of hydration during physical activity.

C9F6043C978847E4A4E82AA33F79A992.description: Compare the balance of good nutrition and physical activity.

7DDD55C17A8E42BEA325B0D6C4168DE8.description: Generate a list of fitness-related activities in which the student participates outside of school hours.

AA91C9BBDEA64628B3305E613513D02D.description: Demonstrate, with teacher direction, the health-related fitness components of cardiovascular fitness, muscular strength, muscular endurance, and flexibility. (Body composition should not be assessed at this grade level and is not recommended.)

6A61108BFE44459CA3B0448475685806.description: Recognize the importance of warm-up and cool-down.

830B339E019B487AA43E69E6927FA67D.description: Describe examples of physical activity which enhances fitness.

691279BEEB8049EAA1738B4F14CBE630.description: Engage in a variety of choices during recess.

5B92FF03D2C547D791D3710EBD4A69D1.description: Participate in activities during class without teacher prompting.

285E24EFA1CF412F96ED43C911D4563A.description: Develop a plan for participation in physical activities outside class.

FD1C36B25A1B41B9AF592D292D8C7222.description: Students will understand the components necessary to maintain a healthy level of fitness to support physical activity.

4D1065D951454E17B3D24F834ED57557.description: Apply simple strategies in fleeing activities.

6D611BEC8D16430BA42B03991BCEF544.description: Apply simple strategies and tactics in chasing activities.

03A65D5962AC49DFB89AFAB52BB2F10B.description: Combine movement concepts (e.g., direction, force, levels, and time) with skills as directed by the teacher.

17B880E78A2149CABB55C10999667D42.description: Apply locomotor skills as they relate to a variety of activities.

4A8246B25E534F8AB3F0C1F2984B932C.description: Recognize open space and how using it will gain advantage.

681B7D0587284EB9AF333CE17D1DC97C.description: Students will apply knowledge to attain efficient movement and performance.

13A7F641D110405BBEA3F592195E7697.description: Perform intermediate jump rope skills using long and short ropes.

4DB221BA3F2E40419149C090891B348F.description: Use a continuous running approach to kick a stationary ball for accuracy.

A3D6E16CE2F3422BBDC6A16E48828631.description: Kick a ball along the ground and in the air while running.

78D81E52F8FA49DC8406B84DF487BF88.description: Receive a passed ball with the inside of the foot and pass to a stationary partner.

2AD871CC026F427F8FD17185FFD590E7.description: Perform a controlled foot dribble in general space at slow to moderate speed.

E3D04ADD8F67435F8F080901E35306A9.description: Dribble and travel with a ball at slow to moderate jogging speed, with control of body and ball.

B47DB0BDCE3A47F3874EA3EA9B38907F.description: Throw an underhand toss to a partner or target with reasonable accuracy.

291710D767E34C55B0EA6E86A882C962.description: Catch a gently tossed ball from a partner.

6B39F66AD2834A24B3B78B8F9F40E2EE.description: Demonstrate balance and weight transfers, using movement concepts to create and perform a dance or rhythmic activity.

DDF5D21705044859A7BA096A35CFDD2E.description: Move in and out of balancing, using curling, twisting and stretching actions.

1B05F74297474A4AA040D35FB61C3707.description: Perform teacher-selected and developmentally appropriate dance steps and movement patterns.

B0EBE5ECCF8241C3A988079514F51FF2.description: Develop jumping and landing in horizontal and vertical planes.

6C1921DF28B04EF5A3695C2D55F5EDE3.description: Establish differentiation between running and sprinting.

5EA855FE2E98445EBCA3CB4CAF9CEAFF.description: Demonstrate leaping, using a mature pattern.

7E307E84EBED463B93EF947537CB6312.description: Students will achieve a level of competency in motor skills and movement patterns.

B97DAD26CCCF40E19A42C08ACE57967E.description: Identify federal and state entities that exist to protect consumers from forms of fraud and abuse.

4566469AE06F465C83380B216A20F64C.description: Explain the purposes and features of consumer protection laws.

17A81CAF471148CDA547D2DA01424941.description: Students will understand the role of government in protecting the consumer.

0D6D42F2594A4EC793AFB53BE8DC3D93.description: Identify the pros and cons of online commerce, including how to conduct transactions safely.

C45188B16DF4462B8728A6EB0A0B9290.description: Describe the negative consequences of gambling and playing the lottery.

FF99DB5C609C46DA84C3F5EDBE6030E8.description: Discuss ways to avoid financial schemes such Ponzi schemes and other questionable and illegal practices.

239B2AD10E0C4E61B2F3F7425B560BA7.description: Understand how to recover from fraud and identity theft.

4B2381CA9A97467B877FFD4E296FB4E4.description: Identify ways to avoid identity theft and fraud, such as securing sensitive financial data, using care when participating in online commerce, avoiding phishing and pharming, and properly disposing of sensitive documents.

D673CD5293E9422EB5933CD39F302B0F.description: Discuss the negative impacts of predatory and payday lending practices.

78545C53B50D4391BDBD9DCE83033AB1.description: Understand financial contracts tied to consumer purchases, such as cell phone, cable or satellite plans, and membership fees.

C09AD361A4FE4FDBA93663039F5B6AB4.description: Define rights and responsibilities of buyers and sellers under consumer protection laws.

6D0181C03C094477BEC4CE1C896A9B04.description: Explain the potential consequences of checking account mismanagement, such as non-sufficient funds (NSF) handling, overdraft processing, and the role of ChexSystems.

446627FDEDBA436B87E56378C7CF53AC.description: Evaluate and identify components of a credit report, including derogatory remarks, and the warning signs of credit abuse, such as late fees, missed payments, collection notices, and bounced checks.

F5FC51340B644B418D9BFFF3D85AE992.description: Understand the legal right to a free annual credit report (AnnualCreditReport.com).

2F9249F0AC1841D6A01DE8510305E346.description: Identify the three major credit bureaus.

23D26BF713EB465489E2E9C1A60CFDCC.description: Explain and understand credit reports and scores.

6E1BACC557234EC2AD1E3A8EBAB62882.description: Describe the personal and societal effects of bankruptcy and identify circumstances that lead to bankruptcy, such as uninsured medical costs, family break-up, or loss of job.

236E535F5F514E1398D80BD699CE09B8.description: Evaluate the costs and risks of payday and predatory lending.

9BB799DB6F33414BA2FEA928A0A4C3FD.description: Locate and use online calculators to determine how principal and interest aggregate monthly for long-term debt such as mortgages, vehicles, personal loans, and credit cards.

E6741EF540DD40AABF6CA109537B1FA0.description: Calculate how long it takes to repay debt by making minimum payments on installment loans and revolving accounts.

927D0BC099114D61A9D3B7B623681B68.description: Describe the risks and responsibilities associated with using credit, such as APR, grace period, late fees, finance charges, default rates, interest, and closing costs.

ED6C074BCED949D7942746C0DC2D3577.description: Explore and discuss the pros and cons of basic types of credit, such as unsecured vs. secured credit, credit cards, installment loans, revolving credit, student loans, and predatory lenders.

2641383B726B45AC930CD5C743A325E4.description: Discuss the purpose and role of credit and explain the value of building and maintaining a healthy credit rating, including elements of creditworthiness: character, capacity, capital, collateral, and conditions.

637BE802990F420AA92A401BD1BDFABC.description: Describe and discuss the impact of credit and debt on personal money management.

BBB6842545834D1C8EDE7121DF447DD4.description: Explain the purpose of co-signers and collateral when applying for a loan.

853DB516DB95462A9CD0BBAC9DEF9B4B.description: Understand the similarities and differences between principal and interest on an amortization schedule.

EF3992BFEFC044108FF24AEC42F3125F.description: Identify the process, rights, and responsibilities relating to renting, leasing, and purchasing a vehicle.

0099FB2BAAFB43C5AD50973DBC522894.description: Identify the process, rights, and responsibilities relating to renting, leasing, and purchasing a home.

F86EE6512E994AF0958689D0E35C5085.description: Emphasize the importance of comparison shopping, buying strategies, negotiation, and sales and marketing strategies in purchasing.

3FA830BFD9554528B97AE406C63AB77E.description: Compare tools for tracking of a budget, income and expenditures, such as the envelope system, paper tracking, and online or software options.

BA7739BBB9194665878F3F1D809F8358.description: List ways and examples of charitable giving.

2EE982D784AB4587B2686D7A591CDF2F.description: Discuss the pros and cons of charitable giving.

F69840F6E871439A8AEC14A179C3742E.description: Emphasize the importance of proactive budget priorities, such as pay yourself first, emergency/opportunity fund, insurance, and charitable or other voluntary contributions.

B62C0DB8B80744059603DCFAE3E3F535.description: Identify and prioritize fixed, variable, and periodic budget categories.

294A2E8074F24D1C9794DCAB16B76949.description: Identify and explain the process of budgeting based on calculated income.

B10C948149854CA7974E90103A1EE2C9.description: Students will understand principles of personal money management, including budgeting, managing accounts, and the role of credit and impacts on personal finance.

FD075386608A477992426ABFC11691FE.description: Understand identification and designation of beneficiaries.

3088E4B12F3B4E26B23BDCB9910FC12C.description: Discuss insurance needs at different stages of life.

39E2C83A7FCF4092B1C1CC88948D599C.description: Define terms of a basic insurance policy, such as contract, limits of coverage, premium, deductible, grace period, and lifetime limit.

3BFD7A1704FB43568B1886CA8CAFF445.description: Define common insurance options and their purposes, such as automobile, health, home owner/renter, whole/term life, long-term care and disability.

7A23A4C7DDC64D8A9F149959BC0C832A.description: Discuss the purposes of insurance/risk management.

619895733FFB44A1B820150D2B9CD8C6.description: Understand the role of risk management in asset protection.

65844341235D40B88208ADC12F0C421F.description: Identify and define the types of financial risks, including inflation, deflation, and recession.
