35EB86F5B1ED41F6B689CED267D9EB88.description: Understand that personal challenges can be positive and reaction can build personal satisfaction through acceptance of feedback, extending effort and not being afraid to ask for help.

79B777B341334F26A7ACD783EFFEE6C4.description: Identify why physical activity participation reduces stress and promotes positive social interaction.

DCB10660CD6C42178D37B578602CD4DB.description: Describe how being physically active leads to a healthy body.

618F4B775C324D84A9B892EC08E54C24.description: Students will appraise the personal value of physical activity as a tool for wellness, challenges, and interacting with appropriate social skills with friends and family.

5EC6E7A5E4A54820AD361E7B8ECD04BD.description: Use physical activity and fitness equipment appropriately and safely, with minimal teacher guidance.

4A6DE19ECB4C4C17A6FA20E0FFCAD70B.description: Demonstrate understanding of rules and etiquette for physical activities, games, and dance.

82E9E0C0A7384172935C25F727AC45D2.description: Demonstrate understanding that there are differences among classmates in physical development, maturation and varying skill levels by providing encouragement and positive feedback to peers.

281683ABF4B44197874F1DE6938A7004.description: Identify and use appropriate strategies to self-reinforce positive fitness behaviors, such as positive self-talk.

8F6D74D588BC4CBB9B8C036D83585833.description: Exhibit personal responsibility by using appropriate etiquette, demonstrates respect for facilities and exhibits safe behaviors.

C07C50BFF0324D2E8D6AC5D19F20766A.description: Students will develop cooperative skills and positive personal behavior through communication and respect for self and others.

F3308CDD9ADB47C68659E8FAD185DE76.description: Identify positive and negative results from stress and appropriate ways of dealing with each.

EA3FFA4BC9CA48FF8767724F8119B6B8.description: Select food within each of the basic food groups, and select appropriate servings and portions for age and physical activity level.

B62EA9892A3A4C9B8691F802DC8C0274.description: Design and implement a program of remediation for any area of weakness based on results of health-related fitness assessment.

FCF7460E1CA348EDA8074C465B9F81C1.description: Explain the role of warm-up and cool-down before and after physical activity.

537AA2D1C8384E44B38C337588092A4B.description: Differentiate between skill-related and health-related fitness.

E361401D67DA4F52A9108E2F6830E3FF.description: Participate in self-selected physical activity outside of physical education class.

1665AA8DF9204D0A88EE15A5E1C4C5BC.description: Record daily activity and identify benefits gained. Describe how being physically active leads to a healthy body.

09F10627DD5A48CFA76A0E093ECD48EB.description: Students will understand the components necessary to maintain a healthy level of fitness to support physical activity.

836D93AA9E78470EA7CF55327CFAF5FA.description: Reduce open space on defense, by making the body larger and reducing the passing angles.

EB3C9969AB684B0DA01452063B6B9DE1.description: Execute an offensive tactic, such as pivots, fakes, or change of direction away from the ball, to create open space.

CF53A92C37A84D0B8B375474DE1D6833.description: Apply speed, direction, and force using a long-handled implement, sending it toward a specific target area while in motion.

78D5A53FCA374CEC97EAD688537ABF2A.description: Demonstrate individual strategies in a small group setting in both defensive and offensive situations to create or deny open space.

4AEAAF4C0EDC4247B3902D7A125347AC.description: Students will apply knowledge to attain efficient movement and performance.

BF183D29AA494648A30C963143BE704A.description: Create a jump rope routine with repeated patterns and combinations of movement.

7408A632585D4C7B8B7F9D8B6A190995.description: Demonstrate a well-developed form of the overhead volley through implementation in a game setting.

10271F1E9BC248749144DD1987FE8C3F.description: Demonstrate a complete skill by dribbling and shooting on goal with power in a game setting.

6D44FC0B421E46F9AC06BBEF7BEA76D2.description: Pass and receive with the feet, using a well-developed pattern in a small group activity.

2CDFEE9FB47C434B99FF91473A58BAA4.description: Complete a variety of practice tasks; dribble with control, changing speed and direction.

93DA65D52E96422087087C46466CB208.description: Dribble with the dominant hand, using a change of speed and direction in a variety of practice tasks.

412C7051475E4B0EA88E3D0293071E2B.description: Execute consistently (i.e., 70% of the time) a well-developed underhand pattern for target games such as bowling, bocci, or horseshoes.

D69130B57F48429AB2B4FA0D58E0FC08.description: Catch a variety of objects from different trajectories, using varying practice tasks.

817430618D07423A8A01303B2DF01E3A.description: Use locomotor and non-locomotor skills to teach a group dance or rhythmic activity.

041C500184D44A0186A4485C9A03ADEE.description: Perform a rhythmic dance using drumming, and incorporate complete movement using ropes, balls, or Lummi sticks.

28608E17125846F78758285CE92924C2.description: Demonstrate correct rhythm and patterns for a dance form (e.g., folk, social, creative, line or world dance).

7AE71642D4994F049D8AC307D913164E.description: Combine movement with manipulative skills to reach a target and score a goal (e.g., soccer, hockey, basketball).

C9B41D047339456C9E7950D47B14E9D3.description: Demonstrate competency in locomotor skills as applied to small group games (i.e., 3-5 players), such as basketball, flag football, and speedball.

402CAC3072AA4B35BD3D0C405EF511AD.description: Create an open space by using locomotor movement and change of speed and direction during activity.

4251F3E916FD40408C56E19941C1CB4B.description: Students will achieve a level of competency in motor skills and movement patterns.

document.title: Utah Core State Standards for Social Studies 2017

D908FC69DAA144E385569171CDF2D6B0.description:
Students will craft an argument for an appropriate role for the
United States to take in addressing a global economic, environmental,
or social issue such as humanitarian aid, migration,
pandemics, or the loss of wildlife habitat.

C1DB5CB3F51B4F21A9A3EC994287D048.description:
Students will evaluate how global economic interdependence
and international trade policies affect the economy of the United
States.

D7336028A41F48248A838E05DF5A5E99.description:
Students will analyze the justification for, and effectiveness of,
specific foreign policy positions, such as military intervention,
isolationism, alliance formation, economic sanctions, or other
security measures.

727D00C6B1274C60955234FA9AAB34FE.description:
Students will analyze the constitutional process of creating
foreign policy and the structures through which the federal
government interacts with foreign governments, such as the
Department of State, treaties, agreements, and alliances.

F046759EE61D4174884403FCC80BCA44.description: The U.S. and Our Relationship to the World

534DFCD7DD624F1A97F8AD4ED407ED9F.description:
Students will propose and defend budget priorities at either the
local, state, tribal, or federal level; and share their findings with
appropriate stakeholders.

3636EF855FD24E48A6188D7AA765D3B9.description:
Students will explain how government services and other budget
priorities are funded through various forms of revenue
streams, such as fees, bonding, and regressive and progressive
taxes, including property taxes, income taxes, and sales taxes.

3D0798FA695044EF92F551F5489697DA.description:
Students will examine the fiscal decisions governmental agencies
must make and the economic philosophies that guide those
decisions.

A183686A77A74275A20497E8947DBDFB.description:
Students will explain how the administrative rulemaking process
functions within the federal system and the extent and impact of
these rules.

8C59E5D38EE842E3B9307E842C3989EE.description:
Students will explain how the individual roles of the members of
the President’s cabinet are designed to meet various purposes in
government.


AA3D6ED853804B0EB0E20B993E45FC86.description:
Students will use data to evaluate election results and explain
election processes and strategies.

68387CCAC32D41138A62882795C38A4D.description:
Students will explain the processes and motivations for how
and why people organize to participate in civic society, such
as developing political affiliations, joining political parties, and
supporting special interest groups and other non-governmental
or non-partisan civic organizations, and evaluate the political
impact of those affiliations.

7D13945142AD4DBCBFA39D69FD2739D9.description:
Students will explain the role that local elected officers fulfill,
such as mayors, council members, auditors, treasurers, surveyors,
assessors, recorders, clerks, sheriffs, county commissioners,
and district or county attorneys and how local government roles
differ from state and federal roles.

73EE720D747B4DE3AF2A061C40C92FF6.description:
Students will explain the distribution of power among national,
state, tribal, and local governments in order to identify how
needs are met by governance systems.

6A77C999EDFA44D48954341689059389.description:
Students will explain the purpose and importance of fulfilling
civic responsibilities, including serving on juries; voting; serving
on boards, councils, and commissions; remaining well-informed;
contacting elected officials; and other duties associated with
active citizenship.

C7994851525045959200CF1B080AFED4.description:
Students will examine various perspectives on a current
rights-related issue; take a position; defend that position using
the Constitution and Bill of Rights, historical precedents,
Supreme Court decisions, and other relevant resources; and
share that position, when possible, with relevant stakeholders.

2C6463039A224CAA8ECF651998EAA999.description:
Students will use historic and modern case studies, including
Supreme Court cases, amendment initiatives, and legislation to
trace the application of civil liberties, civil rights, and responsibilities
spelled out in the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, and other
amendments.

0DCE67E45CB74F559AC98B7966C029F0.description: Civil Liberties, Civil Rights, and Responsibilites

3B6370D52E5548A0BDD5701FB839BA55.description:
Students will explain the organization, functions, and processes
of the United States government, such as the purpose of the
President’s cabinet, the function of judicial review, and how a bill
becomes a law, and apply that understanding to current issues.

4E42AD114B084547A74983B9C5916200.description:
Students will explain how documents, challenges, events, and
ideas such as the rule of law, the social contract, compromise,
the Declaration of Independence, the Articles of Confederation,
Shays’ Rebellion, and the Federalist Papers significantly influenced
the United States Constitution.

6AF0F84C2EAA4CAA891E8E33C3AC5338.description: Students should be introduced to basic coding skills according to their ability level.

7A08C0E76DE24A6DAF7760499A78EA04.description: Students will do activities that help to build creative thinking skills and creative abilities.

25EA9DBAFE664F7D929FF3BD8F4CD270.description: Students will do some introductory communication activities including simple writing projects, storytelling projects, and basic slideshow projects.

ABCD0552135A49ABB39A03039122F38C.description: Students will use computers for basic school skills practice in reading and math.

8116CEA8D56548AFA13A94C491A1F4B1.description: Students will learn the most basic parts of a computer and computer hardware.

899B3C9019C44977A7F962686B800085.description: Students will learn basic computer navigation using the desktop, dock, webpages, links, tabs, and back arrows.

425B73D1CBAE4CF19A4FDF0CB10C3C9C.description: Students will learn basic mouse skills including point, click, double click, click and drag, and scrolling.

D64174A2999D4376B931A48F1A7D753E.description: Students will learn how to care for computer equipment in the computer lab and elsewhere.

8810A15910A64620BE72A128326AD39A.description: Students will learn how to login to their computers using a basic username and password.

6B6CE996E6A4499DA2CE233EAAA67B21.description:
Students will do some basic writing activities using appropriate websites or a word
processing program.

0434ED6D82CD42B5850571A4974C73D2.description: Students will learn and practice the Homerow Keys by the end of 2nd grade.

30FD3AC77DAC4C4583FD48F2051732CC.description: Students will become familiar with the keyboard by doing introductory activities on their computers.

89EC259B2B67428F9144547A102EB978.description:
Students will know how to  respond to inappropriate or uncomfortable content and
contacts.

36161D5B9ECF4A91A37A989D6B3B49CF.description: Students will learn to be kind online and in the real world.

AC1899FD4F6E45EFAE33DCBCB5293D2D.description: Students will understand the importance of telling an adult when troubling things happen.

66F747795B45471D9DF244995C010E9B.description: Students will understand the importance of protecting personal information.

5B406F7721154AF2BAEE5BFBA7683029.description: Students will understand the importance of using tech time wisely.

F2AEEA740ABC44DDA02503E10B7C20DF.description: Students will recognize the consequences that come from poor online choices.

98221EFB83C24B468DA5C01F53DBB9AA.description: Students will understand the importance of being responsible on the Internet.

4B4C4FCC2C794EDDAED60C55005A5F5C.description: Students will describe the costs, benefits, and sustainability of development in terms of poverty rates, standards of living, the impact on indigenous people, environmental changes, gender equality, and access to education.

C4D3075FBB734AD8A521B7BBCD9B6A65.description: Students will cite examples of various levels of economic interdependence between nations and peoples.

BFB9CDECB9E84D01A16AABC3E9E7DE7F.description: Students will explain key economic concepts and their implications for the production, exchange, distribution, and consumption of goods and services.

DB3FF05918FA4510873E219B12D2E890.description: Students will describe and compare the function and distribution of economic activities in primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors.

AFDD061F7F9A4266B8B7FF067A1F68DC.description: Students will explain the essential attributes of a developed economy and the patterns of development that differentiate less-developed from more-developed places.

62FB083FAB254DED81CD7F4D41501F8C.description: Students will explain how cooperation and conflict have many causes, such as differing ideas regarding boundaries, resource control, and land use, as well as ethnic, tribal, and national identities.

594490A8668F424AA04B38DD9DE7E3D1.description: Students will describe and explain the role physical and human characteristics play in establishing political boundaries.

BCC64A00BF0B4682AEBFCC695DC1A500.description: Students will explain why and how people organize into a range of political structures at different scales.

970152886FFB4AC5A13D4F616F9686A3.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of their own culture's connection to geography.

70B511EDB6E04DFCB2CD6FE6F50FE6AC.description: Students will cite examples of how globalization creates challenges and opportunities for different cultures.

A0DDB1A4DE174CE088F2CC9049E063FE.description: Students will explain how the basic tenets of world religions affect the daily lives of people.

D081498E2C964A0FB0DCCEA4D94907B6.description: Students will identify the causes, methods, and effects for the diffusion and distribution of cultural characteristics among different places and regions.

7471425FFC56465A99EB8947A3A77C63.description: Students will identify how culture influences sense of place, point of view and perspective, and the relative value placed upon people and places.

E7317B33BFD3461784C8F2E0960ABBF0.description: Students will explain how the physical environment influences and is influenced by culture.

0116675090CE480F8AA092DE72A6D47D.description: Students will identify and describe the essential defining characteristics and functions of culture.

65B8240C309147F6830E2538EDF073EC.description: Students will investigate the effects of significant patterns of human movement that shape urban and rural environments over time, such as mass urbanization, immigration, and the movement of refugees.

4E9F8AF3402B4111821E5BEED271C445.description: Students will explain push and pull factors causing voluntary and involuntary migration and the consequences created by the movement of people.

65D75966565648C98D284D3375F9A789.description: Students will evaluate the impact of population distribution patterns at various scales by analyzing and comparing demographic characteristics such as gender, age, ethnicity, and population density using maps, population pyramids, and other geographic data.

3BE5A1AA04CC495197C6494C56417CCF.description: Students will use geographic reasoning to propose actions that mitigate or solve issues, such as natural disasters, pollution, climate change, and habitat loss.

8D7BB6D9533E45EBA50ACAEF247055C2.description: Students will cite evidence of how the distribution of natural resources affects physical and human systems.

1BE4FBB30F154EE693B882392BF6375F.description: Students will identify patterns evident in the geographic distribution of ecosystems and biomes and explain how humans interact with them.

667DF7E17EF64E1F969C251F54E5C1B2.description: Students will describe the significant forces that influence the physical environment, such as plate tectonics, erosion, climate, and natural disasters, and explain how the effects of physical processes vary across regions of the world.

39CFFC590B524CE2A0F9618DB5E79445.description: Students will identify a pressing global problem and select the most promising political, technological, medical, or scientific advances being created to address those problems.

0882A6D3DD074A75A5AB2D034A0676FC.description: Students will identify international human rights issues, seek and evaluate solutions, and share their ideas with appropriate public and/or private stakeholders.

B6C9A35E750340C69EEE1DC9CAC138DB.description: Students will use a variety of evidence, including quantitative data, to evaluate the social and environmental impacts of modern demographic trends, particularly population changes, urbanization, and migration.

DEBE5F12532C42C89E24E5D64484C9E7.description: Students will evaluate the role of global organizations, such as non-governmental organizations (NGOs), multi-national corporations, military alliances, and other international civic and political institutions within the increasingly global culture of the world.

E4E360E38C66494E974B414D3D822742.description: Students will make a case for the most significant social, political, and economic consequences of 20th century global conflicts and crises, such as human migration, genocide, poverty, epidemics, the creation of social welfare systems, the rise of dictators, the nuclear arms race, and human rights violations.

7A984B13688642A59F44D43C62181C32.description: Students will use case studies to identify the reach and implications of the Cold War for daily life, such as the Vietnam War, the Great Leap Forward, the Berlin Wall, East and West Germany, NATO, the Warsaw Pact, proxy wars, music, culture, and the Olympics.

0D2D0BB45FA54DC6A700912E3BDE1D6E.description: Students will use primary and other sources to contextualize and explain the intellectual and artistic responses to global conflict and economic instability, such as conservatism, cubism, fascism, liberalism, self-determination, socialism, surrealism, and new forms of music.

FDD514F5321F4D4BA1FA3E9B0077783F.description: Students will explain the political ideas at the heart of decolonization, independence movements, and the formation of new political systems, such as liberation theology, civil disobedience, autonomy, separatist movements, and pan-Africanism.

789D46AEF79B489D887C6FE14FE0B55A.description: Students will identify and compare patterns and tactics of othering and demonization that are evident in selected genocides in the 20th century.

CB5E0C64E45B4ED689A9CF9EDDD79EF9.description: Students will identify cause and effect relationships between World War I, the global Great Depression, and World War II.

EB6B77F739A34E849467444DD7D6D315.description: Students will identify the key ideas and characteristics of current political, economic, and intellectual revolutions such as a contemporary revolution, a social movement, or an independence movement.

D24589FFAC524773A56F790DCD8E2D4E.description: Students will compare and contrast the long-term effects of imperialism on a global scale.

977E095B8C754096AAF705DBE404E8A4.description: Students will use primary sources and evidence to evaluate the influence of leading intellectual movements such as realism, romanticism, capitalism, nationalism, and Marxism.

28F87BDC099C4311B3915D50526B5959.description: Students will use a variety of data to identify push and pull factors affecting migration during the Industrial Revolution.

342FFA8D743D4BEC8DFF68137148E976.description: Students will analyze the underlying and immediate causes and the immediate and long-term effects of the Industrial Revolution on nations that industrialized versus those that did not.

871DC15194394F33AEF32F57D0687605.description: Students will identify the cause-and-effect relationships between absolutism, nationalism, and the political and social revolutions of the 18th and 19th centuries.

EF2D4A5D5D7D4FB99C3876A2BC442F58.description: Students will compile and corroborate primary sources as evidence to explain the impact of global exchange and colonization.

7F8AC85533D54D72ACA33AC5B3BCB789.description: Students will analyze the long-term effects of the Columbian Exchange.

13EEE7743A764FBCB68799FE473EA4DF.description: Students will describe the complex cultures of indigenous societies, such as those in Polynesia, Sub-Saharan Africa, Australia, and the Americas.

756B5115EF38434CA3B9367CBB3A5809.description: Students will develop an interpretation of whether the ideas embodied in movements such as the Renaissance, the Reformation, scientific revolution, and Enlightenment led to a changing balance of world power.

744EB3F86BD946F796931E97DA26B7C0.description: Students will compare the development of Europe's maritime empires with land-based empires such as those of the Ottoman Turks, Chinese, and Russians.

6D5A86FC70CD48D5B3F5C6DC3FDF0FD8.description: Students will identify patterns in the diffusion of technology, writing, religion, political systems, and other elements of civilization, using case studies such as the Chinese impact on Japan, the Arab impact on Mali, the Byzantine impact on Russia, the Roman impact on Europe, and the Olmec impact on later American civilizations.

893DB70FDF664ACABE7E58AB9710ED6A.description: Students will explain the social, political, religious, technological, and economic changes in medieval Europe that created a context for later European colonization.

17B64EF009174F3FB0BA894FB188304B.description: Students will evaluate the long-term effects of the Mongol conquest, such as the diffusion of ideas, technologies, and diseases.

A76966B7460A4C8BB2FE6FF0B3DA9931.description: Students will evaluate historians' interpretations regarding the patterns in the development of civilizations in the Americas compared to other places in the world.

A85D6E4DF28C4FA596C7E30E93105595.description: Students will use patterns in trade and settlement to explain how geographic features such as the Indian Ocean, the Saharan Desert, the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, the Strait of Malacca, and the Mediterranean Sea supported or impeded trade.

C20AF2B7B24E4DB4BD5801494D68B1D1.description: Students will construct an argument for the significant and enduring political, economic, technological, social, or other cultural contributions of classical civilizations.

E67F70FB09D444F4AB3CCA0E10B5D0BE.description: Students will explain the impact of early trans-regional trade on the diffusion of religion, ideas, technology, and other aspects of culture.

FB9B7238169B48DF8CC01BA9D4315B70.description: Students will make evidence-based inferences about the cultural values of classical civilizations, using artistic expressions of various genres as primary sources.

17F95BBC0B844932A9666223CE4EFD1A.description: Students will use primary sources to identify patterns in the stratification of social and gender structures across classical civilizations.

005993B802A8431CA463E18BEEA0944D.description: Students will identify and explain patterns in the development and diffusion and syncretism of world religions and philosophies, including Judaism, Hinduism, Greek philosophy, Confucianism, Buddhism, Christianity, and Islam.

9B5DEF6EB77A423799CC24751162E538.description: Students will compare life before and after the Neolithic Revolution and cite the most significant effects of that revolution on the development of civilization(s).

6366EC5C903B4CE59EEA977F9B146AE1.description: Students will use artifacts and early written records to make inferences about the significance of technological development and diffusion, including writing, in Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Indus River civilization, and the Huang He (Yellow) River civilization.

F92B063DA1CF432594903A13740FCA12.description: Students will use geographic concepts to explain the factors that led to the development of civilization, and compare and contrast the environmental impact of civilizations, pastoralists, and hunter-gatherers.

23EB3F86335F4A6EA56D36F0D0AADEFF.description: Students will analyze the differences and interactions between sedentary farmers, pastoralists, and hunter-gatherers.

92ACA3F524134B55ADA7E464E25DC50F.description: Students will craft an argument for an appropriate role for the United States to take in addressing a global economic, environmental, or social issue such as humanitarian aid, migration, pandemics, or the loss of wildlife habitat.

73FB13C580834CABAB7C2E7AECE95C89.description: Students will evaluate how global economic interdependence and international trade policies affect the economy of the United States.

3522318D841E475B8CFBB24E55F30B24.description: Students will analyze the justification for, and effectiveness of, specific foreign policy positions, such as military intervention, isolationism, alliance formation, economic sanctions, or other security measures.

A3D2AC9FBED543CF838C8C81CCA275B8.description: Students will analyze the constitutional process of creating foreign policy and the structures through which the federal government interacts with foreign governments, such as the Department of State, treaties, agreements, and alliances.

60414CBB05BE4BCA835F4A7CFD7F4C1E.description: The U.S. and Our Relationship to the World

A4A8B5CB47CF4F5AB60AAA5D5489F3DE.description: Students will propose and defend budget priorities at either the local, state, tribal, or federal level; and share their findings with appropriate stakeholders.

AD449DEA724E46FBADD6531E90067D8E.description: Students will examine the fiscal decisions governmental agencies must make and the economic philosophies that guide those decisions.

6153623C04D14AF38E014FF9E7AEF39E.description: Students will explain how the administrative rule-making process functions within the federal system and the extent and impact of these rules.

5D68E4D2E0DA408BB976ADEACCFBF4EF.description: Students will explain how the individual roles of the members of the President's cabinet are designed to meet various purposes in government.

137D52EE8DAC46A28CD6AB1B95DC32EB.description: Students will use data to evaluate election results and explain election processes and strategies.

BE1B19C543D4408690B965A6EA5B0522.description: Students will explain the role that local elected officers fulfill, such as mayors, council members, auditors, treasurers, surveyors, assessors, recorders, clerks, sheriffs, county commissioners, and district or county attorneys and how local government roles differ from state and federal roles.

7D493B8FC51649BD88CB46B63B8A7E50.description: Students will explain the distribution of power among national, state, tribal, and local governments in order to identify how needs are met by governance systems.

EA644CB13D32415D87BDECC2A66B6306.description: Students will explain the purpose and importance of fulfilling civic responsibilities, including serving on juries; voting; serving on boards, councils, and commissions; remaining well-informed; contacting elected officials; and other duties associated with active citizenship

59D97B6F4F784F4DB81A8B1E96F52BFB.description: Civil Liberties, Civil Rights, and Responsibilities

22C94F920F8E4851A94E24C418314CC6.description: Students will explain the organization, functions, and processes of the United States government, such as the purpose of the President's cabinet, the function of judicial review, and how a bill becomes a law, and apply that understanding to current issues.

B0022F831C3C40628A30C590076242E7.description: Students will describe the structure of the United States' form of government as a compound constitutional republic, including the ideas of federalism; checks and balances; separation of powers; commerce, elastic, and supremacy clauses; popular sovereignty; and limited government.

66DC3EF7A8344851A322CA100D8A8261.description: Students will explain how documents, challenges, events, and ideas such as the rule of law, the social contract, compromise, the Declaration of Independence, the Articles of Confederation, Shays' Rebellion, and the Federalist Papers significantly influenced the United States Constitution.

68F7A372E8C94D3A8C3D964EE8596C9C.description: Students will use current events to evaluate the implications of the Civil War and Reconstruction for contemporary American life.

A168FEA0C6C24EC5AFE830EE1585999D.description: Students will compare historians' interpretations of the competing goals of Reconstruction and why many of those goals were left unrealized.

566D78B7EF91478BB2B94B0B1681CE60.description: Students will use evidence to interpret the factors that were most significant in shaping the course of the war and the Union victory, such as the leadership of Lincoln, Grant, and Lee; the role of industry; demographics; and military strategies.

891FAAB4F3914B8A9C6797AE8385B12D.description: Students will explain how slavery and other geographic, social, economic, and political differences between the North, South, and West led to the Civil War.

4952D2BEAA054724870CB9CE609A6B0C.description: Students will make a case for the most significant cultural, political, and economic impacts of territorial and/or industrial expansion.

3DAA5D4358C4441AA752BE7E23D17ADD.description: Students will identify the economic and geographic impact of the early Industrial Revolution's new inventions and transportation methods, such as the Erie Canal, the transcontinental railroad, steam engines, the telegraph, the cotton gin, and interchangeable parts.

AAB6D501C5A64AF6B6812ECAF628FF7F.description: Students will use primary sources representing multiple perspectives to interpret conflicts that arose during American expansion, especially as American Indians were forced from their traditional lands and as tensions grew over free and slave holding territory.

5C7029E55BF94E24855E2E9EE535F226.description: Students will compare and contrast historians' interpretations of the ideas, resources, and events that motivated the territorial expansion of the United States.

E173223854F14AE9BD213601770786CC.description: Students will use case studies to document the expansion of democratic principles and rights over time.

DA30844FA3EC4640B704DFE5C2F441AC.description: Students will identify the conditions that gave rise to, and evaluate the impact of, social and political reform movements such as Jacksonian Democracy, the women's rights movement, the Abolitionist movement, and anti-immigration reform.

3CF57A82C7A94D77BAC950A636FD30FC.description: Students will use evidence to document the development and evolution of the American political party system and explain the historic and current roles of political parties.

4BEE7D9D82FF4788A3ED9263D1D207F1.description: The Development of Political Institutions and Processes

B406FBCA794845DCB3BF04F81E2E46AF.description: Students will use evidence to explain how the Constitution is a transformative document that contributed to American exceptionalism.

1714AC12785048D2B8A00ED16718F913.description: Students will use historic case studies and current events to trace how and explain why the rights, liberties, and responsibilities of citizens have changed over time.

E05E0904CB0E40CB8AE4074408C0DCEB.description: Students will describe the structure and function of the government that the Constitution creates.

482E234A277D4BF3AA9298EF27921B5A.description: Students will explain how the ideas, events, and compromises which led to the development and ratification of the Constitution are reflected in the document itself.

688DC3A8E5E142EE9A741A3AD0BD456E.description: Students will explain how the ideas and events of the American Revolution continue to shape American identity.

F7C9E1F333984173881FEECAF76E449C.description: Students will use primary sources to compare the contributions of key people and groups to the Revolution, such as Paul Revere, Thomas Paine, Abigail Adams, the Sons and Daughters of Liberty, and Thomas Jefferson.

C2E53051B9DA4DA6B9EC3740E7B4F0AE.description: Students will compare and evaluate historians' interpretations of the significant historical events and factors affecting the course of the war and contributing to American victory.

7CF6A294C5BF4D8AB7EF02857985A829.description: Students will use primary sources to identify the significant events, ideas, people, and methods used to justify or resist the Revolutionary movement.

894FF8344813413FACE49AE33E3FC30D.description: Students will explain historic and modern regional differences that had their origins in the colonial period, such as the institution of slavery; patterns of life in urban and rural areas; differences between the French continental interior, Spanish southwest, and English northeast; and the location of manufacturing centers.

749FF3C82CDA47008C447C5B04ED93DD.description: Students will use primary sources as evidence to contrast the daily life and contexts of individuals of various classes and conditions in and near the English colonies, such as gentry, planters, women, indentured servants, African slaves, landowners, and American Indians.

93966BED33D4435C8145EA3CC4122010.description: Students will compare and contrast the economic, political, and social patterns evident in the development of the 13 English colonies.

068DF2174B4A4A4C80024EFAFACDBEF5.description: Students will identify the economic, social, and geographic factors that influenced the colonization efforts of the Dutch, English, French, and Spanish.

FF293351FAB44B9C9A7B826F0A6EF712.description: Students will identify how the period of exploration has affected the current human geography of the Americas, and in particular the role their own cultural background has played.

8C09EE388B454E65AAB2B69ACA64B01A.description: Students will draw from multiple perspectives and cite evidence to explain the effects of European exploration, specifically on Africa, the Caribbean, and North and South America.

09EAC44D6A6645F7AA10B4DB9A461BFB.description: Students will compare and evaluate historians' interpretations of the motivations and conditions that led to European exploration.

4341F4C451804422872DC4A2704621A9.description: Students will analyze evidence, including artifacts and other primary sources to make evidence-based inferences about life among several American Indian nations prior to European exploration of the Americas.

C1FBBFEFFB5D4EC5BDB0F6FB2AA22D52.description: Students will use evidence from recent events and historical precedents to make a case for the most significant opportunities the country will have in the future.

48CAD2F32F5942B7995C191B0D882E10.description: Students will apply historical perspective and historical thinking skills to propose a viable solution to a pressing economic, environmental, or social issue, such as failing social security, economic inequalities, the national debt, oil dependence, water shortages, global climate change, pandemics, pollution, global terrorism, poverty, and immigration.

078E7245BDED4EC3B85BD17C90A37EAD.description: Students will select the most historically significant events of the 21st century and defend their selection.

62F9A4E012D3411D83F4B856BC5776B7.description: Students will use historical events and trends associated with American policies toward Israel and Middle Eastern nations and groups to make suggestions for current policies.

69143B9F10B14DA7BE7EC454085C16CA.description: Students will use evidence to demonstrate how technological developments (such as television and social media), government policies (such as Supreme Court decisions), trends (such as rock 'n' roll or environmental conservation), and/or demographic changes (such as the growth of suburbs and modern immigration) have influenced American culture.

E643DCFD8139472EAEC7A8E6A901B187.description: Students will explain how Reagan's neo-conservatism differed from the policies of previous presidential administrations of this era, most notably Johnson's Great Society.

44AC5F66E13D420989C26602F4FEF824.description: Students will develop interpretations of the impact of the Cold War on American society and culture using evidence such as cultural artifacts from the Cold War era, oral histories, and primary sources.

E7A0BE7BBDE44BD1B0C7CE781DF373C4.description: Students will use government documents and other primary sources to investigate the motives behind a Cold War policy, event, or foreign operation, such as Truman Doctrine, containment, the domino theory, the Korean conflict, the Bay of Pigs invasion, the Cuban Missile Crisis, the Vietnam War, and Olympic boycotts.

7F46028E1615458F9A45B4999E28D8BA.description: Students will compare the causes, major events, military tactics, and outcomes of the Korean and Vietnam Wars.

F33B2D77B4174543B92F7A6827997FD4.description: The Cold War Era and a Changing America

39CF938B115E454BAF8F70F07EA05481.description: Students will evaluate the impact of using international economic aid and diplomacy to secure national interests, specifically citing case studies of America's investment in war-torn nations following the war, such as the Marshall Plan and the Berlin Airlift.

B4515EE8E15A4B59B876AEDCA0EC7589.description: Students will research and prioritize the most significant events in the United States and the USSR's transition from World War II allies to Cold War enemies and superpowers.

FFA497CA167141499FD1F62233A1F5DB.description: Students will cite and compare historical arguments from multiple perspectives regarding the use of "total war" in World War II, focusing on the changing objectives, weapons, tactics, and rules of war, such as carpet bombing, civilian targets, the Holocaust, and the development and use of the atom bomb.

163ECC1EE831491B8B04E89991A6EE9A.description: Students will use primary sources to describe the impact of World War II on the home front and the long-term social changes that resulted from the war, such as the baby boom, women in the workplace, and teenage culture.

D0AB3C9996F44338845A412997389075.description: Students will assess the causes and consequences of America's shift from isolationism to interventionism in the years leading up to World War II.

67818D63424F44C298A6512D79BB1D0B.description: Another Global Conflict and the Beginnings of the Cold War

0E4820B0A9234AF28DDA97360D2848F2.description: Students will craft an argument regarding the role of government in responding to economic conditions after learning about capitalism and other economic systems, historic cycles of boom and bust, and the New Deal.

270786FF99C9491780169DFC0E03828B.description: Students will explain how economic and environmental conditions, including the Dust Bowl, affected daily life and demographic trends during the Great Depression.

2CC792B0F2A249C4A68BB16235D01D7E.description: Students will use evidence to investigate the effectiveness of the New Deal as a response to economic crises.

20784807730847BAB5BE97080BD096CD.description: Students will investigate how individual and institutional decisions made during the 1920s, such as over-production, buying on credit, poor banking policies, and stock market speculation helped lead to the boom of the 1920s and then the Great Depression.

640E1200F79941D4B010D04973677074.description: Economic Boom, Bust, and the Role of the Government

CA56D0FEAC634D1F972BD734F80DB49E.description: Students will identify significant counter-cultural movements of the 20th century as well as the reactions and counter-arguments to those movements, using examples such as the Beatniks, hippies, and the anti-Vietnam War movement.

300764F9589949278B9E497186B4E0A1.description: Students will identify the civil rights objectives held by various groups, assess the strategies used, and evaluate the success of the various civil rights movements in reaching their objectives, paying specific attention to American Indian, women, and other racial and ethnic minorities.

B25DA4A01DD144448E713EB81ABDC525.description: Students will use case studies involving African-American civil rights leaders and events to compare, contrast, and evaluate the effectiveness of various methods used to achieve reform, such as civil disobedience, legal strategies, and political organizing.

83801079134A4B2FBA3E397DC31FE724.description: Students will develop and defend an interpretation of why cultural clashes occurred in the 1920s, citing examples such as science vs. religion, rural vs. urban, Prohibition proponents vs. opponents, and nativism vs. immigration.

6F7BA156E4D5439EB0C73503D2D43B4A.description: Students will explain the causes for U.S. involvement in World War I and the effects of the war on the home front, such as migration, trade, sedition act, shortages, voluntary rationing, and the Spanish flu.

15D9227B3FC247B5BB76FBF26CB6CC5D.description: Students will evaluate the positive and negative impacts of imperialism on the U.S. and the U.S. territorial interests, such as the Philippines, Cuba, Guam, Hawaii, Panama, and Puerto Rico.

DF516A79FD514A58B406174F7336519B.description: Students will examine and evaluate the role of the media and propaganda in promoting involvement in foreign affairs, using events such as the Spanish American War and World War I.

8B3452FDAEB143FA9CEB10CC453842FC.description: Students will describe how the role of the U.S. in world affairs changed at the turn of the 20th century, and evaluate the arguments used to promote or discourage involvement in world affairs, such as those of the "big stick," Mahan, the Roosevelt Corollary, and the Antiimperialist League.

70FAF0212BBE4552900AA7EB595E62F3.description: Students will evaluate the short- and long-term accomplishments and effectiveness of social, economic, and political reform movements.

D01EF7E9565248B2B8D135998AA19833.description: Students will evaluate the methods reformers used to bring about change, such as imagery, unions, associations, writings, ballot initiatives, recalls, and referendums.

1579DA269B9C4DCEAF6550C99C376CF8.description: Students will explain how social reform movements influenced Constitutional amendments and changes to laws and democratic processes.

0FB2E39443BA49FAB22B3CEE0FCBD9EF.description: Students will use primary and secondary sources to identify and explain the conditions that led to the rise of reform movements, such as organized labor, suffrage, and temperance.

3606012BA9F54451A9734964A93E9BC0.description: Students will use historical evidence to compare how industrial capitalist leaders used entrepreneurship, free markets, and strategies to build their businesses.

24A79AADEF50406482337F06D5E63F60.description: Students will analyze the causal relationships between industrialization and the challenges faced by the growing working classes in urban settings.

3964349A5A5A45858F8B0A58CAE3C99C.description: Students will explain the connections between the growth of industry, mining, and agriculture and the movement of people into and within the United States.

2115D1D0B4FD4918B4A83490A21C12CB.description: Students will assess how innovations in transportation, science, agriculture, manufacturing, technology, communication, and marketing transformed America in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

620AF325116944FB83A4084BC8B06D47.description: Students will research issues of civic importance in which city, county, tribal, or state governments have a role. Students will use their research to develop and write a policy proposal to the appropriate governmental entity, such as a board, commission, council, legislator, or agency. (civics)

BC3A15440C7643EF9064C602512A45A4.description: Students will use recent population growth and other demographic trends to make predictions about Utah's growth, and create and defend a public policy in response to those trends. (economics)

809DAFE2C1584A58B83007E708D7251F.description: Students will use data regarding the key components of Utah's economy to make recommendations for sustainable development. (economics)

721B4C681AEF42A8B99A45F4DC07D279.description: Students will use geographic tools and resources to investigate a current issue, challenge, or problem facing Utah or their community, and propose a viable solution. (geography)

ECC4631A0DB14246B514DFF5E5DEEBF1.description: Students will select a recent event they think will be worthy of remembering, recording, or interpreting, and make an argument for its potential historical significance. (history)

1589D9B9F73B4C6D9E1DFA599FB1CCBD.description: Students will evaluate the impact of tourism on Utah's economy and geography, such as the development of tourism industries, state and national parks, and events including the 2002 Olympics. (economics)

C29B109CB9024CDC89F0B7533683BE30.description: Students will describe the historic and present management of natural resources and make recommendations for natural resource management in the future. (geography)

E8D6179B81AD47F28C2BCDCD7D6522D9.description: Students will use data and other evidence related to a cultural, ethnic, or religious group in Utah to interpret the group's historic/current conditions and experiences. (history, geography)

351135762B7C4C439991E01FF15EA5B6.description: Students will describe the economic ties between Utah communities, the nation, and the world. (economic)

8ED335DB07B644899208D10D1498BEB3.description: Students will make an evidence-based argument regarding the appropriate roles of local, state, and federal governments in resolving a current and/or historical issue. (civics)

6F79F74D934E445B804894DF6808FD42.description: Students will evaluate the impact of the Cold War on Utah, such as the uranium boom, nuclear testing, nuclear waste storage and disposal, and the MX missile controversy. (history)

BA27A9A474C84B39A895D1D7A8246AB2.description: Students will identify the causes and effects of the Progressive movement using examples from community or state history, such as the organized labor movement, tax reform, the Scofield mine disaster, and education and child labor reforms. (civics)

7084B9058E874459945A084E00620E22.description: Students will describe the effects of events, movements, and innovations on Utah's economic development, such as the organized labor movement, farming and industrial improvements, the World Wars, and the Great Depression. (economics)

36199E40D7D44802861CF88FB1AF400B.description: Students will use primary sources and/or oral histories to analyze the impact of a national/global event such as World War I, the Spanish flu epidemic, the Great Depression, World War II, and Japanese American internment on an individual or community in Utah. (history)

2C09F2348AC443ECAF55AC610CB4BDD2.description: Students will identify the civic virtues and principles codified by the Utah Constitution. (civics)

C310F63FC5D1486AAA0671DD1167ACDB.description: Students will explain how their own connection to Utah is a reflection of the complex history of the state. (history)

76979BD376E24A8993171077CA7D6156.description: Students will identify the political challenges that delayed Utah's statehood and explain how these challenges were overcome. (civics)

0FF48C94899E4D5EA876ACDFF636E518.description: Students will explain how agriculture, railroads, mining, and industrialization created new communities and new economies throughout the state. (economics, geography)

44DF06AB93814857A9C38655133EF6D5.description: Students will construct an evidence-based argument to explain how the development of transportation and communication networks across the state changed Utah's economy and human geography. (economics, geography)

17FA9DB086414272992C4698C2E76547.description: Students will research multiple perspectives to explain one or more of the political, social, cultural, religious conflicts of this period, including the U.S. Civil War and more localized conflicts such as the Utah War, the Mountain Meadows Massacre, the Bear River Massacre, the Black Hawk War, or other Federal-Mormon conflicts. (history)

BFEDFC7FC72C484B9B78C94E5A5F5015.description: Students will use geographic inquiry to explain patterns in the settlement of Utah and the subsequent trends in urbanization, referring to a range of communities as case studies. (geography)

4568FD1B54A949C5892FA08B6681FC7D.description: Students will compare the causes and lasting effects of various non-Mormon groups' migrations to Utah. (history)

87B960CC230F415FA84E6A36B983FDFA.description: Students will explain the causes and lasting effects of the Mormon migration to Utah. (history)

1F40C39EA23C4AA2B44A069BFC4A6713.description: Students will describe the cultural change and continuity of at least one of Utah's current sovereign nations as it has responded to changing political, social, and economic forces. Students will use a variety of resources that may include written primary and secondary sources, oral histories, photographs, artifacts, and art. (economics, civics)

0CF922E9420247F2BD3D08763A9BD974.description: Students will analyze primary and secondary sources to explain causes and effects of European-American exploration, including the response and involvement of Utah's American Indian tribes. (history)

CDEC918CC0B340F8A9E4D9CBBD8EB5A4.description: Students will explain the economic activity of a prehistoric and/or historic American Indian tribal community by using basic economic concepts, including supply, demand, trade, and scarcity. (economics)

E90A048B2DEB4A70AFC7B3A5E3BAA4E9.description: Students will analyze and explain the interactions and interconnections between the physical characteristics of Utah and American Indian cultures using a range of texts, oral histories, and geographic inquiry. (geography)

C0E55885E69849B9A3CD4775965C0E58.description: Students will make evidence-based inferences about the complex ancient cultures in Utah after studying artifacts from the prehistoric era. (history)

18232A2E3D9C4E26894F6D9203652B4B.description: Relate artistic ideas and works with societal, cultural, and historical context to deepen understanding by analyzing how art reflects changing times, traditions, resources, and cultural uses.

4C4A7948656B43A7AF30D722DE37936F.description: Generate a collection of ideas reflecting current interest and concerns that could be investigated in art-making.

63897766EA1A46BCA7057989EA63647A.description: Connect: Students will relate artistic skills, ideas and work with personal meaning and external context.

36923C3B47A84F1F955BE4C67966C8B0.description: Develop and apply relevant criteria to evaluate a work of art.

34948FB7112249C597AF9999CB451E35.description: Interpret art by distinguishing relevant contextual information, and by analyzing subject matter, characteristics of form and structure, and use of media to identify ideas and mood conveyed.

2CB37CB6C209448EA6B1B77260C1D737.description: Analyze ways that visual components and cultural associations within images influence ideas, emotions, and actions.

606B7641EF2847C896C208F38607A214.description: Compare one's own interpretation of a work of art with the interpretation of others.

958B34734ACD43BBB9EB6BD1AA1B91CD.description: Identify and interpret works of art or design that reveal how people live around the world and what they value.

CC8698399C2148D1B9DFA85332B922AA.description: Respond: Students will understand, evaluate, and articulate how works of art convey meaning for the observer as well as the creator.

7223D186CDFA4B65BA9D7E8C55B16A2D.description: Assess, explain, and provide evidence of how museums or other venues reflect history and values of a community.

90579639FFBB41AF9371A3AF98ED40CA.description: Individually or collaboratively develop a visual plan for displaying works of art, analyzing exhibit space, the needs of the viewer, and the layout of the exhibit.

7585B8B52BE841BAA7113D9B691D1B79.description: Analyze the similarities and differences associated with preserving and presenting two-dimensional, three-dimensional, and digital artwork.

735366682BE04173AA3B1FDA2B629977.description: Present: Students will analyze, interpret, refine, and select artistic work for presentation. They will convey meaning in the manner in which the art is presented.

69140FA7E4904FCEAADDCF2A0394ECC3.description: Reflect on whether personal artwork conveys the intended meaning, and revise accordingly.

9033D6BC1D9C45F1811E4F3BB2E4644D.description: Design or redesign objects, places, or systems that meet the identified needs of diverse users.

35569CA77D7D4745B115A9991D3BB679.description: Explain environmental implications of conservation, care, and cleanup of art materials, tools and equipment.

E535D4B072D04176A465008103BDD1BB.description: Demonstrate openness in trying new ideas, materials, methods, and approaches in making works of art and design.

857D43C047C644C9A8DEE45648F1DC2F.description: Formulate an artistic investigation of personally relevant content for creating art.

9A96E6FBD1FD4A97860D1747C7BF1695.description: Combine concepts collaboratively to generate an innovative idea for art-making.

05DA038557E248D2BC71A2420E5D5087.description: Create: Students will generate artistic work by conceptualizing, organizing, and completing their artistic ideas. They will refine original work through persistence, reflection, and evaluation.

0C903118E4FB4B469C5B512297F27A42.description: Experience and explore music which connects us to history, culture, heritage, and community; identify connections between a music genre and cultural or historical contexts; and explore and explain how musical works are influenced by a composer's heritage and experiences.

5DBF7999C6804E2F9249C79CEE0EE7AF.description: Draw upon interests, knowledge, and skills developed to inspire and inform the creation, performance, and appreciation of music, and deepen understanding of another content area through music.

83CBA1C4D08543998AF6D55DD0EE2236.description: Describe how music relates to personal, social, emotional, and intellectual development.

3F6911035AEA4778B8C0A58673AFC792.description: Connect: Students will synthesize and relate knowledge from personal and collaborative experience to make and receive art. They will relate artistic ideas and works with societal, cultural, and historical context to deepen understanding.

9CEBD6FC821440EF817BBBEBD432B64B.description: Apply teacher-provided or collaboratively developed criteria to evaluate musical works or performances.

CCCDC0965AE648F0A7C2E2A88D941862.description: Identify and describe the technical and musical skills evident in a quality performance.

107CF60DCC254901B14608E465E39687.description: Identify and describe the music and structural elements that contribute to a quality work or performance.

D903F40A447A47379BFF3440B5C7EBF5.description: Identify music elements that are characteristic of different genres of music.

A44A5FB3D5B54011B7DCA0CDF43FCCD4.description: Explore/express feelings conveyed by a music selection through movement, drawing, or writing.

79E803C1D63349F1950970363E641DFD.description: Identify possible intent of a music selection, and how the music elements are used to convey it.

A86684928A444A048344794B5A86DB81.description: Describe feelings or imagery conveyed by a music selection.

51EA92599CFD4D55AC9F3CCBFC62C6E4.description: Demonstrate audience etiquette appropriate for the context and venue.

520444B631104D68B533E93FB7F9A4B8.description: Listen for and identify form, meter, rhythm, timbre, dynamics, tempo, melody, texture, and harmony/tonality.

BD9EF2D4DD34424B97BE447BFB0130B7.description: Listen to and interact with a variety of contrasting music.

DB6AD35E3C8C405CBE34B042892B2789.description: Respond: Students will perceive and analyze artistic work and process. They will interpret intent and meaning, and apply criteria to evaluate artistic work and process.

89F05B99FBA5422A910E493370A5B10D.description: Perform music with expression, technical accuracy, and appropriate interpretation; watch and respond to the conductor to perform dynamics, style, and phrasing, and start, stop and stay together; and demonstrate performance decorum.

955A41111EC34157B38DFF2C7DF37197.description: Demonstrate persistence and cooperation in refining performance pieces.

41C2071D8CE64C4297BBC82E0C053B2F.description: Respond to musical terms and markings for tempo and dynamics.

2B76CDC2960B46909219E96023B62281.description: Respond with body percussion, voice, or simple instruments to visual representation of rhythm patterns.

34C25CC171874932B8C2A2D18BFA2181.description: Perform and identify rhythm patterns in two-, three-, four-, and six-beat meters using body percussion, voice, and simple instruments.

ECAAA03BDD4E45EBB570C887830CEBED.description: Perform two- and three-part rounds, partner songs, descants, layered ostinatos and parallel harmony.

AE5DAD5E5C5649E2B0383238171E6A5C.description: Respond to visual representations of melodic patterns using pentatonic, major, and minor scales.

3C973EAE9FA34913ADD5DD3A16FD6346.description: Sing folk, traditional, and rounds in tune, with good vocal tone and clear diction.

DAE53F8293924FBB8A533BEA00D02353.description: Discuss and explore, with guidance, expressive elements in music to be performed.

DBBDBD00BB994C6BB9D1E4A87BEB54EF.description: Make interpretive decisions, with guidance, regarding the use of musical elements to express ideas and emotions.

6EA5CBA52CE3448586F25B65B94B2190.description: Apply teacher-provided criteria for selecting music to perform for a specific purpose and/or context, and explain why each was chosen.

67121F193BB842E5B29EF1ECAF02F448.description: Perform: Students will analyze, interpret, and select artistic work for performance. They will develop techniques and concepts to refine artistic work, and express meaning through the presentation of musical works.

BEC9DAFFA9EF4C3A9323627993727B7F.description: Evaluate and refine work, applying teacher-provided criteria and collaboratively developed guidelines; explain rationale for making revisions; and present the final version of created music and explain expressive intent.

19C02B137A024536AC6D5DC9946FD5D1.description: Use standard or iconic notation or recordings to document original rhythmic, melodic and harmonic ideas.

BE2899FFBD934A5E91DEFE2825F8BF8F.description: Select and demonstrate developed musical ideas for arrangements and compositions within recognizable form, and explain intent and connection to purpose and context.

919E4B3AB6E9440A960B71E1717B5824.description: Improvise rhythmic and melodic patterns and musical ideas, explain connection to specific purpose and context, and generate musical ideas using specific tonalities, meters, and simple chord changes.
